output: Manchester City captain Vincent Kompany criticizes the Financial Fair Play (FFP) regulations, asserting they protect established clubs rather than preventing teams from going bankrupt. Last year, City was fined £50 million and required to limit their transfer spending this season due to FFP violations. In contrast, Manchester United spent £150 million on new players despite being in debt to the tune of £400 million. Kompany claims FFP stifles competition among lower-tier teams aiming to challenge the established elite.

Bath rugby club has signed England Sevens international Jeff Williams for the upcoming season. The 26-year-old has scored 36 tries on the World Series circuit and was a key player in England's recent Tokyo Sevens victory. Born in South Africa, Williams previously played for Hamiltons club in Cape Town and France before joining Bath. The team's coach expects Williams' high-tempo style of play and dynamism to complement their attacking ethos.

Jared Leto has been cast as the Joker in the 2016 film "Suicide Squad," marking his first appearance as the character on the big screen since Heath Ledger. The film, which does not feature Batman, also stars Will Smith, Margot Robbie, and a variety of other villains and anti-heroes. "Suicide Squad" is set to release in theaters on August 5, 2016.

Florida corrections officers Thomas Jordan Driver (25), David Elliot Moran (47), and Charles Thomas Newcomb (42), along with a trainee, have been charged for conspiring to murder a former inmate upon his release. The men were allegedly plotting revenge against the ex-inmate following a previous conflict. An FBI informant, infiltrating the Traditional American Knights of the Ku Klux Klan, discovered the plan. The plot was hoaxed by staging a fake homicide scene and taking photographs as evidence, leaving the three suspects satisfied with the results, but now they face up to 30 years in prison if convicted for conspiracy to commit murder. Florida Attorney General Pam Bondi condemned the violent hate crime.

The conference call for Manny Pacquiao's media event discussing his upcoming fight with Floyd Mayweather was abruptly cancelled due to technical difficulties caused by a high number of boxing writers and broadcasters joining the call. Pacquiao managed to answer only one question before the call was cancelled. The call has been rescheduled due to the technical issues, while Mayweather is due to address the media in a conference call on Wednesday.

The Miami Open has seen two tennis stars, Serena Williams and Andy Murray, being honored with large celebration cakes for achieving significant milestones in their careers. Serena Williams advanced to the semi-finals after defeating Sabine Lisicki in three sets, and will now face Simona Halep. Meanwhile, Murray's cake was presented to him for winning his 500th match, but no upcoming matches are mentioned for him. The tournament has become notable for its generous cake deliveries.

The world's largest terminal, Terminal 1 at Beijing International Airport (also known as Daxing Airport), is set to open in 2018, aiming to accommodate the significant rise in Chinese tourists traveling globally. Designed by Zaha Hadid and ADPI, the terminal will offer a spacious and open layout with a flowing roof design and a central multi-layered courtyard. The project, which will cover 700,000 square meters and cater to 45 million passengers annually, is part of an effort to showcase rich Chinese culture on a worldwide stage. This comes as Chinese tourist numbers and spending have drastically increased since 2000.

Manchester United's manager, Louis van Gaal, confirmed that Wayne Rooney sustained a knee injury during the Premier League match against Everton. Rooney was replaced by Robin van Persie in the 88th minute of the game, which ended in a defeat for United, leaving them in fourth place in the race for Champions League qualification. Van Gaal expressed concern about the severity of Rooney's injury, as United prepare for upcoming games against West Brom, Crystal Palace, Arsenal, and Hull.

Jack Wilshere, an Arsenal midfielder, was shopping for his groceries during a day off, indicating a return to fitness may be near. His instagram post revealed items like Seriously Fruity Mixed Berry Crisp, Oats and Honey Special K, eggs, baked beans, and corn in the cob in his overflowing trolley. Wilshere humorously shared his shopping experience on his social media, asking followers for help with unloading the trolley.

A Venezuelan woman, Marleni Olivo, threw a mango with her phone number on it at President Nicolas Maduro, who was riding a bus, during a rally. The president, finding humor in the incident, displayed the mango on live television and promised to help Olivo with her housing problem. Critics have called the incident a "manguicidio," a play on words meaning the assassination of a powerful leader. However, Olivo clarified that her action was not meant to harm the president and was simply a desperate attempt to solve her housing issues.

Carlos Tevez, a former Manchester United and City striker currently playing for Juventus in Serie A, believes it is more challenging to score goals in Italy compared to the Premier League. He criticizes the Premier League midfields as non-existent and praises the standard of defending in Serie A. Despite sitting out Juventus' defeat to Parma ahead of a Champions League quarter-final, Tevez asserts that scoring goals in the current season is much more difficult. He also expresses his belief that his current Juventus team is more rounded compared to past teams he played for, implying they have a higher chance of repeating the success, such as winning the Champions League.

Yaya Toure, a Manchester City midfielder, was criticized by Jamie Carragher for allegedly ducking away during a free-kick situation which led to Crystal Palace's winning goal, thereby costing City the chance of salvaging a draw at Selhurst Park. The incident, during which Toure was part of a five-man wall, was highlighted by Carragher as unacceptable, particularly given Toure's £200,000-week salary. Carragher, a Sportsmail columnist, suggested that Toure's lackluster response compared to his teammates was a significant contributing factor to the goal. The defeat left City nine points behind Chelsea, who also have a game in hand.

A 50-year-old Australian man died unexpectedly while on holiday in Kuta, Bali, at the 101 Legian Hotel. He collapsed after expressing feelings of illness and was unable to be revived, with doctors suspecting a heart attack. Kuta, a popular tourist destination for Australians, is known for its long sandy beach, varied accommodation, and numerous restaurants and bars. Authorities are working to determine the exact cause of death, with an autopsy still pending.

Former Australia cricket captain and commentator Richie Benaud passed away last Friday at the age of 84 due to skin cancer complications. A private funeral attended by close family and friends, including ex-players Shane Warne and Ian Chappell, was held in Sydney on Wednesday. Prime Minister Tony Abbott had offered a state funeral, which was declined by Benaud's wife, Daphne. The funeral was followed by a memorial service at the Australian Golf Club, with tributes pouring in from cricket fans worldwide admiring Benaud's distinctive voice and commentary style. Benaud, who was considered one of the most influential cricket identities of the past century, played 63 tests for Australia but gained more recognition for his long-spanning career in the commentating booth.

A 16-year-old girl named Isobel Attwood has been missing for two days. She is believed to be with a man in his 20s, potentially in the Winchester or Southampton areas. Friends on social media claim she is safe but needs space, and police are appealing for help to find her, expressing concern for her welfare.

Manchester City players stand to lose significant bonuses – around £500,000 per player – if they fail to qualify for the Champions League this season. This is due to incentivized contracts aimed at adhering to financial fairplay rules. After losing to Manchester United in the latest Manchester derby, City are now in fourth place, just ahead of Liverpool by four points, with the top four finishers securing a place in the Champions League. The team's disappointing performance in the second half of the season, marked by seven losses including exits from the FA Cup and Champions League, has prompted manager Manuel Pellegrini to lament the season's deterioration. Notable players such as Sergio Aguero, Yaya Toure, Joe Hart, and James Milner could miss out on hefty paydays if City don't finish in the top four. The club faces a challenging schedule ahead, including matches against West Ham United, Aston Villa, and Tottenham Hotspur, among others. Meanwhile, Louis van Gaal, the manager of Manchester United, is optimistic about attracting top-class talent in the upcoming transfer window.

Martin Skrtel, the Liverpool defender who has made over 200 appearances for the club since 2008, has dismissed rumors linking him to a move to Wolfsburg or Napoli. Skrtel's agent has confirmed that the 30-year-old is not entertaining any offers from these clubs and is instead working on finalizing a new contract with Liverpool. Despite Liverpool's disappointing season, Skrtel is planning to stay with the Premier League side.

A CEO from Texas, Cheryl Rios, has faced criticism for stating that a woman cannot be president due to the 'hormones' that would supposedly hinder her from starting a war. She made the comments on Facebook following Hillary Clinton's announcement of her presidential candidacy. Despite the backlash, Rios maintains her opinions, stating that she supports women's rights but holds traditional beliefs about the presidency being a male role. She defends her remarks but clarifies that her stance does not extend to the abuse or inferiority of women.

1. Atletico Madrid striker Mario Mandzukic was injured during a physical Champions League quarter-final match against Real Madrid, suffering a cut to the nose from an elbow by Sergio Ramos and a punch to the stomach by Dani Carvajal. Despite his injuries, Mandzukic is expected to play in the second leg at the Bernabeu on Wednesday.
2. Mandzukic missed Atletico's La Liga match against Deportivo La Coruna due to his ankle injury but is now back in training and showed marks from the encounter with Ramos.
3. According to coach Diego Simeone, Mandzukic is the favorite to play in attack alongside Antoine Griezmann, who has been in impressive form and scored both goals against Deportivo.

Jose Mourinho mistakenly believed Marouane Fellaini would play against Chelsea due to a misunderstanding with a hotel doorman, who said Fellaini was there to get tickets from Eden Hazard. Upon finding out Fellaini's twin brother Mansour was at the stadium, Mourinho confirmed it was him posing as Marouane. Despite the mix-up, Fellaini did play in the match, which Chelsea won 1-0, moving them closer to the Premier League title. Kurt Zouma was given tactical instructions to contain Fellaini during the game.

A woman identified as Dawn Milosky from Beachwood, New Jersey, was rescued from an overturned, burning vehicle in Kinnelon. Police arrived at the scene after receiving a tip-off about erratic driving. The woman, initially unconscious, was quickly freed from the wreckage and administered CPR. She was charged with DWI, having an open container of alcohol, reckless driving, and failure to stay in the right lane. Despite the incident, she is reportedly doing well and was airlifted to Morristown Medical Center. The vehicle caught fire just 2 minutes and 30 seconds after she was removed from the wreckage.

A Chinese farmer at Chaohu, Anhui Province, is gaining national attention for a six-legged goat kid born on his farm. The animal, named 'spider goat', was born with four forelegs and two hind legs. Despite initial doubts about the kid's survival, it is growing healthily with an extraordinary appetite. The farmer, Xiao Qibin, decided to let the goat grow naturally and is currently taking care of it daily. The cause of the mutation remains a mystery to the farmer.

West Ham United is reportedly interested in signing Javier Hernandez from Real Madrid this summer, as the Mexican striker, who scored a crucial goal against Atletico Madrid, is out of favor at Real and will return to Manchester United at the end of the season. Hernandez might cost around £7 million. West Ham is focusing on a list of young transfer targets for their final season at Upton Park, with Pedro Obiang, Moussa Konate, and Fabian Schar from Sampdoria, FC Sion, and Basle, respectively, among their top choices.

1. Manager Stuart McCall of Rangers has dismissed any discussions about his future before the end of the season, emphasizing that his current revival of the club has yet to achieve anything significant.
2. McCall's tenure has seen the club win three consecutive matches, including victories over Hibs and Hearts, restoring a sense of optimism and unity among fans.
3. A loan move for Shane Ferguson from Newcastle United is imminent, but McCall is cautious about the Northern Ireland international's readiness due to a long-term knee injury, suggesting he may need to play in Under-20 matches before being ready for first-team action.

Werder Bremen secured a 1-0 win against Hamburg SV, thanks to Franco Di Santo's 84th-minute penalty, keeping Bremen in contention for a Europa League spot. Hamburg's Valon Behrami was sent off at this crucial juncture, and their new coach, Bruno Labbadia, endured a losing debut. The victory moved Bremen up to seventh place, while Hamburg remain in last place, with both teams having five matches left in the season. Hamburg aims to avoid relegation for the first time since the inception of the Bundesliga in 1963, with Labbadia in charge. Top-placed Bayern Munich maintains their lead by defeating Hoffenheim, while VfL Wolfsburg, in second place, seeks to reduce Bayern's advantage when they face Schalke 04 later on Sunday, and Bayer Leverkusen is in third position after a win against Hanover 96.

A two-year-old boy fell approximately 10-12 feet into a cheetah exhibit at the Cleveland Metroparks Zoo after his parents dangled him over the edge. The child, who sustained minor injuries, was rescued by his parents before emergency responders arrived. The cheetahs did not approach the parents or the child during the incident. The zoo plans to press child endangerment charges against the family.

A Russian TV channel rated Hillary Clinton's first campaign video as suitable for mature audiences due to concerns it might violate Russia's anti-gay propaganda law. The two-second clip of a gay couple holding hands prompted the 18+ rating from TV Rain channel. The law restricts the discussion of gay rights and relationships in the presence of minors. The law, which sparked international outcry upon its passing in 2013, is seen as discriminatory towards the LGBTQ+ community.

Siem de Jong, who recently recovered from a collapsed lung, returned to action playing 45 minutes for Newcastle Under-21s. However, he was substituted at half-time during their 2-0 loss to Derby County and may not be fit for the game against Tottenham. Meanwhile, the game saw at least three significant happenings: Derby scored twice in the second half to win; Adam Armstrong had a header wide for Newcastle; and Facundo Ferreyra substituted in for De Jong. Ferreyra, a forgotten Argentinian striker on loan from Shakhtar Donetsk, has been plagued by injuries since arriving last summer.

Chef Ally Lees of Alfie Bird's restaurant in Birmingham has created a three-foot, 12,000-calorie omelette using 150 eggs as an Easter promotion. The omelette, which contains 945g of protein, is more than 16 times the recommended daily amount for a man. Chef Ally suggests that a group of no fewer than five is needed to consume this massive omelette due to its size and high protein content. The omelette cooks for an hour in a large paella pan.

Three Olympic gold medalists, Jessica Ennis-Hill (heptathlon), Mo Farah (10,000 meters), and Greg Rutherford (long jump), will participate in the Sainsbury’s Anniversary Games in London this summer. Notably, Ennis-Hill became a national hero by winning the heptathlon at the London 2012 Olympics. Tickets for this three-day event featuring top-tier athletes, including the world’s only two-day Diamond League meeting and the Sainsbury’s IPC Athletics Grand Prix Final, are now available for purchase. Ennis-Hill is set to make her first public appearance since giving birth last year.

A snack bar in Rio de Janeiro was found to be using the meat of stray dogs for the fillings of traditional Brazilian pastries, known as "pastels." The owner, Chinese Van Ruilonc, confessed to rounding up the dogs from the city streets and using them as a food source. In addition to this revelation, police discovered a worker living in slave-like conditions, imprisoned in a cage with dead dogs and forced to work 18 hours a day without pay. The eatery is alleged to be part of a larger network of pastry houses, including one in the tourist district of Copacabana, owned by Chinese businessmen.

The article details an incident where Ebony Dickens, using the pseudonym Tiffany Milan on Facebook, posted a threatening rant against white police officers. In the post, she expressed support for black-on-white killings and indicated a specific plan to kill 15 white cops. The post was removed the day before Dickens was arrested, and both local and federal law enforcement, including the FBI and Atlanta police, were involved in tracking her down. Police found a firearm and three computers in her home during a search, and Dickens was charged with disseminating information regarding terrorist acts. A judge set her bond at $10,000 and barred her from social media.

PSV Eindhoven celebrated a long-awaited Dutch championship win after a 4-1 victory over Heerenveen on Saturday, with striker Luuk de Jong scoring two first-half headed goals. The triumph ended Ajax Amsterdam's four-year reign as champions. Missing from this season's title race, Ajax will now focus on their Europa League campaign. Meanwhile, bottom-placed Dordrecht moved closer to relegation, losing 3-0 to Vitesse Arnhem, while AZ Alkmaar secured Europa League playoff qualification with a 3-1 home win over ADO Den Haag.

An 11-year-old boy named Shiva was beaten to death by the head teacher of a school in Railamau village, India, allegedly for stealing a pencil and eraser. The teacher, Lalit Verma, has been arrested for culpable homicide not amounting to murder. This incident is said to be the latest in a series of reported cases of teachers physically abusing students in India, with similar incidents occurring in Burdwan, West Bengal, and Bareilly, Uttar Pradesh.

A gastrointestinal illness has affected approximately 100 passengers and crew members on the Celebrity Infinity cruise ship, with symptoms including vomiting and diarrhea. The Centers for Disease Control (CDC) is currently investigating the cause of the illness, and two CDC staffers are scheduled to meet the ship in San Diego on Monday. Notably, this is the third time the Celebrity Infinity has experienced an outbreak of gastrointestinal illness, with previous incidents occurring in 2006 and 2013.

A Boston Terrier named Gizmo has performed an unusual trick, walking on his paws while standing upright, which his owner filmed after Gizmo tried on a new pair of boots. In the footage, Gizmo takes steps while continuously propelling his hind legs vertically, showing a graceful and circus-like movement. The video has been watched more than 80,000 times and has left viewers with smiles on their faces. The owner suspects that the trick was at attempting to adjust to the new footwear.

New Orleans has implemented a smoking ban in most locations, including bars, casinos, and restaurants, following a unanimous vote by the city council in January. This decision aims to protect workers from second-hand smoke. Some bar owners and patrons expressed concerns about potential revenue loss and the loss of smoking spots, leading to a lawsuit being filed to challenge the ban. The ban came into effect on the 1st of February, and violations will incur fines starting at $50. Notably, this change will not affect popular tourist attractions such as visiting Treme or eating beignets.

Manchester United Under-21, captained by Adnan Januzaj, achieved a comeback victory over West Ham United in the Under-21 Premier League, going four points clear at the top. The game started with West Ham taking a surprising early lead through Oxford's header from a Cullen cross, their first away goal since September. However, the Red Devils equalized quickly, with Josh Harrop scoring two goals, the second secured by taking advantage of the West Ham goalkeeper's poor handling. Januzaj had a notable impact on the game, coming close to scoring on multiple occasions from free-kicks. The decisive third goal came when Harrop cheekily volleyed in the ball.

Brisbane's Anglican Archbishop, Phillip Aspinall, has joined a local Catholic priest in advocating for Queensland's controversial 'gay panic' homicide defence to be abolished. In his Easter Sunday mass sermon, Archbishop Aspinall supported Father Paul Kelly's stance on removing this defence, stating that violence is never a suitable response to sexual advances. Furthermore, Archbishop Aspinall also addressed incidents of violence at anti-Islam rallies and church vandalism, encouraging compassion and resistance to fearful responses.

Sandra Bullock, aged 50, has been named the world's most beautiful woman of 2015 by People magazine. She humorously labels the accolade as "ridiculous" and emphasizes the value of inner qualities such as kindness, good parenting, and laughter over physical appearance. The cover story features Bullock's home life with her son, Louis, 5, and her personal efforts to maintain health and fitness beyond her 40s. The selection of Bullock, the oldest woman to receive this title, is seen as a sign that beauty transcends age.

On Monday morning, an improvised bomb exploded near a U.N. vehicle in Garowe, northeastern Somalia, killing six people, including four aid workers from UNICEF. The bomber, who was among the U.N. staff, also died in the attack. Somalia's President denounced the attack as an assault on the country's future, particularly its children. This incident follows a separate ambush in the Lower Shabelle region on Sunday, where three African Union troops were killed. Al-Shabaab, a terrorist group affiliated with Al Qaeda, claimed responsibility for Monday's attack.

A Texas wildlife park operator named Gary Saurage, resembling a modern-day Crocodile Dundee due to his baseball cap, was called to capture a massive 400-pound, 11-foot-long alligator residing in a family's backyard pond. In the capture, Saurage is seen approaching the aggressive beast with his bare hands and looking directly into its eyes. The alligator, later found to be a 35 to 40-year-old male, was eventually hauled out of the pond safely but required significant effort due to its aggressive behavior. Remarkably, this was not Saurage's largest catch—his biggest alligator, nicknamed Kong, measures 12 feet and 6 inches. Saurage advises that people should not fear these toothy lizards as long as they maintain a safe distance and never attempt to feed them, since alligators can run up to 22 miles per hour on land, a speed humans can't match.

In eastern Turkey, five members of the Kurdistan Workers' Party were killed, and another was wounded in clashes with Turkish armed forces. Four Turkish soldiers were also wounded in the fighting, which occurred in the city of Agri. Prime Minister Ahmet Davutoglu and President Recep Tayyip Erdogan condemned the violence, with Erdogan describing it as an attempt by Kurdish separatists to intervene in the ongoing peace process. Recently, Abdullah Ocalan, the leader of the Kurdistan Workers' Party, called from his prison cell for an end to the violence and urged followers to lay down their arms.

Two 18-month-old twins tragically died after accidentally falling into a canal in Yuma, Arizona, on Friday morning. The area where the canal is located is commonly used by families for walks and jogging. Investigators are probing the incident but do not suspect foul play. The boys were rescued after more than an hour, flown by a U.S. Marine Corps helicopter to a Yuma hospital, where they were later pronounced dead.

Orlando City, an MLS team with a significant Latin-American following, is reportedly interested in signing Manchester United's Javier Hernandez, who is currently on loan at Real Madrid, as he struggles for playing time. Hernandez could be a commercial draw for Orlando, coached by Adrian Heath. at the same time, multiple European clubs have also shown interest in Hernandez, including Premier League teams Southampton, Stoke, West Ham, and Everton, as well as Wolfsburg, AC Milan, Lazio, and Inter Milan. Separately, Manchester United has made a revised contract offer to 19-year-old Andreas Pereira, who has attracted interest from several European clubs, including Paris St Germain, Juventus, PSV Eindhoven, and Feyenoord. Pereira was on the bench for Manchester United's game against Aston Villa on Saturday.

Couple Joel Burger and Ashley King, both 24, got engaged, with Ashley accepting the proposal. Known as "Burger King" since a motivational speaker noticed the clever name combination in fifth grade, the New Berlin, Illinois, natives plan to humorously incorporate their Burger King nickname into their wedding, intending to serve drinks in personalized Burger King cups at their wedding, if the restaurant chain allows it.

A 1960s hit band, unnamed in the article, was identified in a 1964 police intelligence report as attending a pedophile brothel in Battersea, South West London, the same location frequentered by disgraced BBC star Jimmy Savile. It's unclear whether the band and Savile visited the brothel at the same time. The investigation into the brothel was initiated in 2013 by Detective Superintendent David Grey as it was mentioned in another police report. The DJ passed away in 2011, following public disclosure of his allegedly extensive secret life involving pedophilia, and it is not specified whether any investigation or evidence linking the band and the pedophile activity were initiated.

A German Shepherd named Sadie, from Alberta, Canada, was filmed playing an electric keyboard, using her paws to press keys and her nose to turn it on. Despite seeming to struggle with the rhythm at one point, Sadie continues her performance gesturing signs of frustration before outright bowing and turning away after 20 seconds. The viral video has received positive comments from viewers, and Sadie's owner shares that she enjoys learning new tricks, including playing the piano, which the owner adopted her from an animal shelter six years ago.

A man named Ivan Balashov, while browsing smartphones in a store in Novokuznetsk, Russia, took a selfie using one phone but preferred another. He attempted to leave the store with the preferred phone but was stopped by security. The security guard at first let him go, but Balashov ran away. Police identified Balashov from the selfie and traced him to his home, where he denied any involvement with the store. However, they found proof of his presence in the store just 30 minutes earlier. Balashov was later convicted and given a three-month suspended sentence.

The first trailer for the documentary "Amy: The Girl Behind the Name" has been released, showcasing the life and music of Amy Winehouse who struggled with drugs and alcohol during her career. In the trailer, Winehouse expresses ambivalence about fame, stating she doesn't think she would be able to handle it. The film, which has been endorsed by Winehouse's family, will feature unseen archive footage and previously unheard tracks, and is set to release in the UK on July 3. The filmmakers aim to portray not just the great artist Winehouse was, but also her funny and loving personality. The film's US release date remains undisclosed.

1. "The Big Bang Theory" features the return of Christine Baranski and Laurie Metcalf as the mothers of two characters, promised to be a standout episode.
2. Scarlett Johannsson is hosting "Saturday Night Live" on NBC on May 2nd, a day after the release of her new blockbuster "Avengers" movie.
3. Allison Janney continues to deliver Emmy-worthy performances in the underrated dramedy "Mom", with its season finale this week.

1. Fans of Downton Abbey may still see the character Violet, Countess of Grantham, played by Dame Maggie Smith, as her younger self in a new American show named The Gilded Age, set in 19th Century New York.
2. The series, created by Julian Fellowes and airing on NBC, could potentially feature other Downton Abbey characters like Robert, Earl of Grantham, and his American-born wife Cora.
3. The Gilded Age, focusing on the robber barons and industrialists of the late 19th Century, is being considered a potential replacement for Downton Abbey and might air as early as September, with production starting after Fellowes finishes work on Downton Abbey's sixth and final series.

Steven Gerrard, who is nearing the end of his career with Liverpool, has been selected to play in the FA Cup semi-final against Aston Villa at Wembley Stadium. This will be his 36th and potentially final game at Wembley, marking his return from a three-match ban for a red card against Man United. Gerrard, described as a "special player" by manager Brendan Rodgers, won his first FA Cup in 2006 and Liverpool's last trophy at Wembley in 2012. Rodgers has spoken highly of Gerrard's contributions to the team, with the player known for producing key performances in important games.

A new, original Dr. Seuss book titled "What Pet Should I Get?" is set to be released on July 28, featuring the spirited siblings from "One Fish Two Fish Red Fish Blue Fish." The first printing of the book has been increased from 500,000 to 1 million copies due to high demand, and it marks the first new, original Dr. Seuss book since "Oh, the Places You'll Go!" in 1990. The manuscript for the new book was found in the authors' California home after his death in 1991 and is believed to have been written between 1958 and 1962.

Jessica Carey surprised her grandmother, Patty Lawing, by getting a tattoo of a childhood portrait of her on her forearm. The tattoo was uncannily accurate, showing Patty as a young woman with long red hair, wearing a smart blouse and jacket. The surprise was captured on film, with Patty reacting emotionally, overwhelmed by the gesture. The video emerged online in February, with Jessica sharing it, expressing her fondness for her grandmother and the priceless reaction to her meaningful tattoo.

Annegret Raunigk, a 65-year-old mother of 13 from Berlin, is due to break the record as the oldest woman to give birth to quadruplets. She is currently 21 weeks pregnant following 18 months of fertility treatment and is expecting the babies in the coming weeks. Despite the high risks associated with quadruplet pregnancies, particularly in women of her age, she expressed confidence in her ability to handle the delivery and has decided not to terminate the pregnancy. Raunigk made headlines previously in Germany for giving birth to her youngest daughter Leila at the age of 55.

Japan's space agency, JAXA, plans to deploy an unmanned rover, the SLIM probe, on the moon by 2018, aiming to perfect soft-landing technologies for potential future manned expeditions to the moon or even Mars. Estimated to cost around $83.4 million to $125 million, the mission, if approved, will utilize face recognition software to help the rover identify craters on the lunar surface. This move is seen as Japan's attempt to keep pace with rivals China and India, who have achieved significant extraterrestrial milestones in recent years. The lunar landing site will be determined based on data gathered by Japan's previous moon mission, SELENE (Kaguya), which orbited the moon in 2008.

The article reports that Brazilian football clubs, including Corinthians, Palmeiras, and Santos, are on alert due to a dengue fever outbreak affecting some of their players. Paolo Guerrero from Corinthians, Aranha from Palmeiras, and Leo Cittadini from Santos have been diagnosed with the mosquito-borne disease and are expected to miss several games due to recovery. Teams have been advised to take precautions such as using insect repellent during practice and inspecting their training centers for breeding sites of the mosquitoes that carry dengue. This year, cases of dengue fever have increased significantly in Brazil, with over 460,000 cases reported by the health ministry, causing nearly 5,000 cases a day and more than 130 deaths.

James Wilson, a Manchester United striker, expressed admiration for his teammates' specific qualities, revealing he would most like Wayne Rooney's free-kick skills, Robin van Persie's movement, and Radamel Falcao's predatory instincts. He praised Rooney's regular practice and accuracy in free-kicks, Van Persie's ability to create space and receive the ball, and Falcao's knack for being in the right place at the right time. Wilson has 16 appearances for United this season, scoring one Premier League goal.

In Milwaukee, Wisconsin, a tragic incident occurred on Sunday evening. Archie Brown Jr, a father of four, was struck and killed after hitting a 2-year-old who ran into the street. Shortly after, an unidentified gunman opened fire at the scene, fatally shooting Brown Jr and a 15-year-old boy, whose connection to the incident is unclear. Police believe the shooting may have been in retaliation for the child's death, though they are still investigating and have yet to identify any suspects. The victim, Archie Brown Jr, was a real estate entrepreneur and landlord, leaving behind four daughters, the youngest only six months old.

A minor boy from Memphis, Tennessee has gained over 3,000 Twitter followers by posting pictures and videos that depict alleged 'gang life,' including gun possession, smoking suspicious substances, and vulgar language. This has sparked criticism from Twitter users and members of the community, with some expressing concern for the boy's well-being and calling for him to receive help and education. The boy's mom has stated that the backlash is stressful for her, and the boy has defended himself by claiming he's had a difficult year and his sister has been incarcerated for two years. The increasing use of social media, including Twitter, is becoming a concern for authorities in perpetuating gang culture, with approximately 50% of organized gangs in the US maintaining a social media presence.

John Schumann, the former Redgum frontman, has criticized anti-Islam protesters for using his song, I Was Only 19, at a Reclaim Australia rally. Schumann, who wrote the 1983 anthem as a call for compassion, tolerance, and inclusiveness, expressed disappointment over the song being co-opted by the movement. The song, honoring all Australians who have served their country, was not meant to promote ignorance and intolerance, especially ahead of the Anzac centenary. The rallies across Australia resulted in violent clashes between the group's supporters and anti-racism groups, leading to several arrests, including in Melbourne.

Emmanuel Adebayor, a striker for Tottenham Hotspur, has declared his intention to stay at the club and compete for a place, despite recent reports suggesting a move away. He labels the Premier League as the best in the world and voices thanks for the opportunity to play there. However, his performance this season has been underwhelming, with only two goals in 16 appearances, and with the emergence of Harry Kane, his future role with the team is uncertain. His last Premier League goal for Tottenham was against Newcastle in October 2015.

1. Stuart Pearce argues that Manchester City manager Manuel Pellegrini should be given more time to improve Manchester City's faltering performance, as the team faces a tough battle to secure a top-four finish and has been reduced to a dejected look in recent weeks.

2. Pearce, a former Manchester City player and manager, cites the inconsistency of Yaya Toure as the primary reason for the team's poor performance, claiming that the Ivorian's declining form and scheduling conflicts during African Nations tours have contributed to the club's struggles.

3. Despite the club's underperforming squad this season, Sergio Aguero has emerged as a bright spot for Manchester City, delivering promising performances.

Hull City manager Steve Bruce is optimistic about keeping the team in the Premier League despite a 2-0 defeat against Southampton, as they now face tough upcoming fixtures. Hull played better for the first half but ultimately lost due to a penalty and a late goal. Bruce attributes the team's struggles to several long-term injuries affecting key players such as Mohamed Diame, James Chester, Michael Dawson, Nikica Jelavic, and Robert Snodgrass. Meanwhile, Southampton coach Ronald Koeman had to intervene after Sadio Mane attempted to take a penalty, breaking team rules.

A fake missile with a dummy wearing a balaclava was discovered on a boat sailing on the Thames in Reading, causing a terror alert. The police and bomb disposal team were alerted, but later confirmed the missile was ornamental. A local resident criticized the prank, stating it was insensitive due to the potential for causing panic amidst ongoing terror concerns.

Tiger Woods endured a bizarre injury on the ninth hole at the Masters when he inadvertently struck a tree root with his club during a swing, causing an apparent ligament injury in his right wrist. Despite the pain, he managed to complete the competition at 5-under-par. Jordan Spieth, 21, dominated the tournament from start to finish, marking the first time in 39 years that this has been achieved; he ultimately won the Masters. Woods ended up tied for 17th, finishing 13 strokes behind Spieth, but this was his best finish in over a year.

Iker Casillas, currently at Real Madrid, has stated his intention to stay and fight for the No. 1 jersey, despite speculation linking David de Gea from Manchester United as a potential replacement. Casillas, who has been with Real Madrid since his teenage years, aims to honor his contract and train hard for the position. In the meantime, Casillas is focused on helping the team retain their Champions League title and acknowledges the competitive nature of the final stages, which include Barcelona, Bayern Munich, and Juventus.

In Russia, a S300 missile launch failed spectacularly, with the rocket barely taking off before plummeting back to Earth. The incident resulted in a small explosion followed by a large plume of smoke, potentially causing embarrassment to President Vladimir Putin given the recent increase in the Russian defense budget. Remarkably, a second OTR-21 Tochka missile was launched from the wreckage soon after. This incident occurred in a region near Donetsk, Ukraine, where the missile was believed to be aimed at government forces.

Australian World Cup winner James Faulkner has been signed by Lancashire as their overseas player for most of the summer. Faulkner, who was named man of the match in the World Cup final against New Zealand, will replace compatriot Peter Siddle after his Indian Premier League stint. Lancashire head coach Ashley Giles is thrilled about the signing, noting Faulkner's impressive first-class cricket record and expressing excitement about his potential contributions to the team.

1. Mary Kay Letourneau Fualaau, a former 34-year-old teacher who served jail time for an illicit relationship with her 13-year-old student Vili Fualaau, is set to appear in an interview on ABC's "20/20" this Friday.

2. The couple, who married in 2005 and have two teenage daughters together, will celebrate their 10th wedding anniversary on May 20. In the interview, Mary Kay will discuss what keeps their marriage strong despite their age gap, her intentions to return to teaching, and her efforts to have her status as a registered sex offender lifted.

3. Vili Fualaau, now 31, will discuss his personal battles with alcoholism and depression, and why he believes the legal system failed him during his time as a minor.

Ex-Liverpool player and soccer analyst Jamie Carragher traveled to Spain during the international break to watch his son James play in the Under 12s division of the Mediterranean International Cup in Girona. Carragher attended the opening ceremony and watched as the Liverpool U12s team drew 1-1 against CE Mercantil, with the Reds facing CE Cristinenc and FE ATL Bisbalenc in their Group E games. Notable players such as Philippe Coutinho, Lucas, Lionel Messi, Cesc Fabregas, Neymar, Gerard Pique, Oscar, and Juan Mata have previously participated in the tournament.

Seattle-based filmmaker Gabriel Ng, during a three-month stay in Thailand, used a drone to film a six-minute love letter video showcasing the country's stunning beauty spots, including the picturesque coastline, religious sites, everyday life scenes, and islands like Ko Samui and Ko Phan. Notable attractions captured in the video are Wat Phra Yai (Big Buddha Temple), peaceful rivers, mountains, and waterfalls. The high-definition video, shot with a £500 drone and a GoPro, has received acclaim on YouTube for its Discovery Channel-like quality.

Peter Moores, currently England's coach, expressed a willingness to work with Michael Vaughan, a potential new director of cricket for England, despite a past disagreement. Moores did not express the need for another voice in the team and was sad about the departure of Paul Downton, a key figure who brought Moores back to coaching. The focus remains on the upcoming Test series.

Nottingham Forest are planning to reinforce their attack by making a renewed offer for Blackburn Rovers' Jordan Rhodes this summer, priced at £10 million. Previously, Forest manager Dougie Freedman attempted to sign Rhodes on loan with a view to a permanent deal, an offer that was rejected by Blackburn in March. With 70 goals in the last three seasons, Rhodes is a coveted forward. Additionally, Blackburn's strike partner, Rudy Gestede with 19 goals this season, is attracting interest from Hull, Crystal Palace, West Brom, and Southampton.

In Bahama, North Carolina, three dogs - a Husky named Sky, and two Springer Spaniels, Sadie and Marshall - performed a spontaneous musical act by howling and barking in harmony. The performance consisted of Sadie initiating the barking, followed by Sky joining with a more melodious howl, with Sadie then also howling. Marshall, the third dog, moved about excitedly in response. The video ends with the owner calling for quiet, and the surprised dogs briefly stopping their performance. The resulting sound was a combination of barks, howls, and growls.

The 'French Spiderman', Alain Robert, climbed Dubai's 1,007ft twisted skyscraper, the Cayan Tower, without a safety harness, using only sticky tape and chalk for assistance. Hundreds of spectators watched as Robert scaled the 75-storey tower, which has a twist of 90 degrees, in an hour and a half. This marks Robert's second climbing feat in Dubai; he has previously been arrested, imprisoned, and banned from various locations worldwide for illegal ascents.

1. An experimental cancer drug discontinued due to poor cancer treatment results, AZDO5030, has shown promise in reversing the effects of Alzheimer's, as revealed in a study conducted at Yale University.

2. The treatment achieved this by blocking a process that breaks nerve connections in the brain used for memory storage, and consequently, restored memory in mice affected by Alzheimer's.

3. Human trials for the drug have been initiated to test its efficacy in Alzheimer's patients, led by researchers Stephen Strittmatter and Christopher van Dyck, as efforts continue to combat the growing issue of Alzheimer's in the UK, with 850,000 people already affected.

1. Paul Bettany will play the Vision, a long-anticipated member of the Avengers, in the upcoming "Avengers: Age of Ultron" movie.
2. Several new superhero projects were addressed in the article, including the reveal of Ben Hardy as Angel in "X-Men: Apocalypse," and a first look at Charlie Cox's Daredevil suit in the upcoming Netflix series.
3. The expected appearance of Jamie Bell's The Thing in the rebooted "Fantastic Four" movie was also confirmed, with the character's appearance reportedly enhanced by CGI.

Veteran referee Kenny Bayless, who has worked several of Floyd Mayweather and Manny Pacquiao's fights, has been appointed as the third man in the ring for their highly anticipated match. However, some, including Oscar De La Hoya, a past opponent of Mayweather, express concerns that Bayless' appointment might unintentionally favor Mayweather, as De La Hoya suggests Bayless has a habit of breaking up fights in a way that benefits Mayweather. This concern arises due to Bayless' tendency to break up fights when both fighters' hands are tied up, even without throwing punches, which De La Hoya suggests could be an advantage for Mayweather.

Harry Kane's potential involvement in the Under 21 European Championship is uncertain due to Tottenham arranging a post-season friendly in Malaysia, scheduled for May 27. Spurs manager Mauricio Pochettino worries about burnout and desires Kane to rest for the following season, despite the striker expressing his desire to play for Gareth Southgate's Under 21 side. Kane recently captained Tottenham in a 0-0 draw with Burnley, but despite his early goal in his England debut last month, his inclusion in upcoming international fixtures appears unlikely.

The California measles outbreak that started in December, affecting over 130 individuals, has been declared over by the California Department of Public Health. This was determined as there has been no new case of the B3 strain of measles for 42 days, which equates to two incubation periods. Of the 81 patients for whom vaccination status was known, 70% were unvaccinated. Health authorities attribute the control of this outbreak to prompt investigations, interviewing of contacts, vaccinations, and increased awareness among healthcare providers about measles. The initial outbreak originated from visitors to two Disney theme parks in December. Since then, two patients with rashes have been identified in April, but they have a different measles genotype, as there are 19 different strains discovered since 1990. Measles is a highly contagious respiratory disease that can cause serious health complications such as pneumonia and encephalitis, and it is spread through coughing or sneezing and can remain in the air and on surfaces for up to two hours.

A family-of-six was sighted in San Miguel de Tucuman, Argentina, riding on a single motorbike without helmets. The arrangement included a man holding the handlebars, three young children on the petrol tank, a girl and a woman on the seat behind him. This incident follows a similar instance of a family of seven on a motorbike in Junin, Argentina. Both instances were met with public condemnation for endangering the children's safety, and authorities are currently seeking the parents involved.

Andrea McVeigh, a 44-year-old social media manager, was seriously injured after being knocked down by a cyclist on the pavement in Bermondsey, south London. The cyclist fled the scene, but CCTV footage has been released by the Met Police in an attempt to identify the cyclist. McVeigh sustained significant facial injuries, including two three-inch gashes to her forehead, and is currently off work sick and feeling scared to venture outside. The incident has been condemned by local police, who have expressed sympathy for the victim and pledged to identify the cyclist responsible.

The headstone of Hillary Clinton's father, Hugh Rodham, was found tipped over in Scranton, Pennsylvania, two days after Clinton announced her run for the White House. The gravestone is located at the Washburn Street Cemetery, and it's the caretaker, Paul McGloin, who first noticed the vandalism. Police are currently investigating, suspecting vandalism, but are also considering the possibility of a weather-related incident. McGloin believes the coincidental timing of the incident and Clinton's announcement is noteworthy.

A California woman, Beatriz Paez, was terrified when a Deputy U.S. Marshal took her cell phone during a recording of police activity, smashing it with his foot. The incident occurred in South Gate, California. Paez has since filed a complaint and is considering a lawsuit. The U.S. Marshals Service is reviewing the incident, and U.S. Representative Janice Hahn has written a letter to outgoing U.S. Attorney General Eric Holder, requesting a federal investigation into the officer's actions, as Paez was not hindering an investigation or arrest.

Max, a husky-corgi mix, is currently residing at the Dogs Trust in Basildon, Essex, having been abandoned. Despite his small stature, Max is a fully-grown dog and is described as gentle, intelligent, and big-hearted. The rise in popularity of huskies, partly due to shows like Game of Thrones, has led to an increase in the number of these breeds being cared for, with many later being abandoned due to owners not being prepared for their specific needs.

Chilean pickpockets have surpassed other groups to become the most effective thieves in central London, targeting wealthy shoppers in the West End. They are known for operating in groups of three to six, often appear as families or businessmen, and are particularly skilled, making them difficult to trace. Local police are aggressively monitoring these gangs, with many arriving on a six-month visa and moving through various European cities to avoid detection.

A 20-year-old man survived a severe car accident where his vehicle flipped over and landed on him, trapping him. Firefighters used 25 minutes to free him from the car. The man suffered head, chest, and possibly leg fractures but miraculously remained conscious. Emergency services, including multiple ambulances, fire engines, police, and the Warwickshire and Northamptonshire air ambulance responded to the accident scene in Southam, Warwickshire. The man was airlifted to the University Hospital Coventry and Warwickshire with multiple injuries including head, chest, pelvic, and leg fractures. The ambulance service praised the quick response and early treatment efforts by their community paramedic at the scene. Firefighters used technical equipment to free the man from the wreckage.

A gang of fly-tippers dumped an estimated 40 tonnes of industrial waste in a Suffolk village, leaving a massive pile that is the worst case of fly-tipping seen by a rural crime officer in almost 30 years. The rubbish, including materials from the carpet and veterinary industries, was transported using three tractors and trailers. Police, National Farmers' Union, and Country Land and Business Association are currently working to clear the waste and prevent future incidents.

A man was Tasered at Pearson International Airport in Toronto after refusing to comply with security protocol, attempting to enter a restricted area, and aggressively trying to board a Turkish Airlines flight. The incident was captured on video, revealing the man's non-responsiveness and visible shake followed by police bringing him to the ground. The man was later transported to a hospital under Canada's Mental Health Act, and it remains undecided whether criminal charges will be filed.

An incident forced a government jet carrying Serbia's president to turn back during a flight to Italy last week. The cause was traced to a co-pilot spilling coffee on the instrument board, which activated the emergency slat button, causing the plane to tumble and lose altitude. The pilot managed to regain control, but one engine stopped working before the plane safely returned to Belgrade, resulting in the temporary suspension of the co-pilot's license.

In South Africa, over 300 suspects have been arrested for deadly attacks on foreigners that forced thousands to flee; the government condemns these attacks and praises law enforcement for stopping further bloodshed. These attacks occurred in Durban, where mobs with machetes targeted immigrants, killing two immigrants and three South Africans. The South African government implores citizens to remember the country's history of overcoming challenges with the support of African neighbors and encourages unity. The Gift of the Givers charity is providing support to those seeking refuge, with over 8,500 people having fled to refugee centers or police stations due to the violence. In the past, Johannesburg has also been the epicenter of anti-immigrant tensions, with similar violent attacks happening in 2008.

A skier, Zach Birnie, was caught in an avalanche while skiing off-piste in Revelstoke, Canada. The incident was recorded on a helmet-mounted camera. As he began skiing slowly and making a controlled turn, his skis became buried in snow leading to a minor avalanche behind him. Panicking, he was pushed down the mountain by the heavy snow, panicked, and subsequently became fully submerged in the snow. After the avalanche, he re-emerged, shook off the incident, and wrote online about the accident describing it as the best and worst case scenario. Cornelia Accola from the WSL Institute for Snow and Avalanche Research SLF suggested that the avalanche may have been caused by fresh snow and steep terrain. She provided advice on how to escape from a similar situation: let go of ski poles, try to open bindings, pull knees toward chest, and hold arms in front of the face to try and escape the avalanche area.

On the hottest day of the year, two men robbed an Esso petrol station in Surrey, stripping off their shirts before the robbery. The men entered the manager's office of the filling station in Caterham, looking for cash. Surrey Police have released CCTV images of the men in hopes of identifying them, announcing that a third man has been arrested and released on police bail while the investigation continues.

The article discusses the Lada Niva 4x4, a rugged and affordable 4x4 vehicle produced by the Russian automaker Lada. Given the end of Land Rover Defender production, there is a possibility of increased sales for the Lada Niva, which has already gained a cult following due to its robust nature and distinctive appearance. The Niva is a simple, no-frills vehicle with a plastic interior that is easy to clean after off-road adventures, but it was formerly equipped with a German engine in a model driven by Russian President Vladimir Putin in 2009.

The AIDS Healthcare Foundation, the nation's largest HIV and AIDS medical care provider, is being accused of a $20 million dollar scam involving kickbacks for patient referrals in a lawsuit filed by three former managers in South Florida federal court. The lawsuit claims that employees were offered $100 bonuses for referring patients with positive test results to the company's clinics and pharmacies, with the alleged practice starting in 2010 at the company's California headquarters and expanding to multiple locations. The company, which cares for over 400,000 patients in 36 countries, denies the allegations and asserts its actions are crucial for HIV detection and treatment.

A bearded dragon named Liz appears to understand English as she nods when asked "Are you hungry?". The reptile, owned by Shannen Hussein, is known for its conversational skills and enthusiasm for superworm treats. Shannen Hussein, who also manages an online-famous pet lamb named Winter, also cares for numerous other pets on her hobby farm, including cats, birds, a snake, ducklings, turtles, a llama, and possibly an emu. After eating, Liz is seen looking very content.

A West Virginia resident, Travis Hatfield, has gained viral fame for his heartfelt rendition of a George Jones hit to his uncle, Jamie Joe Cline, who has Down syndrome. The video, which has garnered over 410,00 views, showcases their weekly musical bonding. Travis, a aspiring country singer, is now receiving offers from Nashville record labels due to the video's popularity, with plans to audition for 'The Voice' 2016 season and release a CD of original songs. Jamie, who has lived with Travis for over a decade, is a key source of inspiration for Travis' musical ambitions.

High-wire artist Nik Wallenda has announced plans to walk untethered on top of the Orlando Eye observation wheel, which is part of a new entertainment complex in Orlando, Florida, on April 29. This feat will be performed as the wheel is in motion. Wallenda, a seventh-generation member of the Flying Wallenda family, has previously performed death-defying walks such as across the Grand Canyon and Niagara Falls, and twice between Chicago skyscrapers without a net or harness, the second time while blindfolded.

Bayern Munich central defender Medhi Benatia faces an absence of between two and four weeks due to a muscle injury, which may rule him out for both legs of their Champions League quarter-final against Porto. The injury is a setback for the team, as Benatia joins a growing list of injured players including Bastian Schweinsteiger, David Alaba, Javi Martinez, and Tom Starke. Despite these injuries, Bayern Munich is still aiming for domestic and European success, and key players such as Franck Ribery and Thiago Alcantara have recently returned to training.

Bayern Munich, managed by Pep Guardiola, clinched a berth in the Champions League semifinals after a 6-1 victory over Porto, bringing their season goal tally to an astonishing 115 goals. With five Bundesliga matches remaining, three Champions League matches if they reach the final, and the German Cup semifinal against Borussia Dortmund, they're aiming for a potential 141 goals for the season. Key goals in the season so far include Thiago Alcantara, Robert Lewandowski, Sebastian Rode, Mario Götze, Arjen Robben, Jerome Boateng, Holger Badstuber, and more.

Former Atletico Madrid striker Fernando Torres has credited manager Diego Simeone for the team's recent success, which has led to them becoming one of the most respected sides in Europe. This is evident in their six consecutive wins against Real Madrid, including the Super Cup, King's Cup, and both league clashes. Torres emphasizes Simeone's leadership and awareness of the team's strengths and weaknesses as crucial factors. Meanwhile, five Atletico players, including Torres, are one yellow card away from a suspension for the return leg of the Champions League quarter-final against Real Madrid.

A small aircraft en route from central Scotland to Tiree, the most westerly island of the inner Hebrides, crashed near Loch Etive in western Scotland, resulting in the discovery of the bodies of two passengers. Search and rescue operations involving lifeboats, helicopters, and the police were launched after the plane lost radar contact near Beinn Nan Lus. Police are investigating the circumstances of the crash and urge anyone with information to contact them.

A bus crashed into a Boeing 777 jet, believed to be an Uzbekistan Airways service, at Tashkent airport, Uzbekistan. The damage is apparent, but details about potential engine damage or injuries are unavailable. This incident, which delayed many passengers, is unfortunate and has become more common, with similar occurrences happening at other airports, such as Dublin Airport with Ryanair planes. In 2014, a Ryanair jet had its winglet torn off in a collision at the same airport, and in January 2021, a British Airways plane hit a hangar at Heathrow Airport. In all these instances, there were no reported injuries.

An off-duty Secret Service agent, Arthur Baldwin, was arrested in Washington D.C. early Friday morning on charges of attempted burglary and destruction of property. Baldwin was posted with the Foreign Missions Branch of the service, which works with the State Department on diplomatic activities. His arrest follows another high-ranking official being put on leave for misconduct allegations, both incidents are currently under investigation. These recent incidents add to the ongoing challenges facing the Secret Service, responsible for protecting the president and his family.

Israel is developing a cutting-edge tunnel detection system, jointly created by Elbit Systems and the Israeli Ministry of Defense, to prevent false alarms. The system, predicted to cost around £2.3 million ($3.5m) per mile, will primarily focus on the land border between Gaza and Israel and is aimed at providing additional security. The project, following years of conflict between Israel and Gaza, has successfully passed initial tests but the exact timeline for implementation has not been specified.

A primary school headteacher, Linda Shute, has implemented a policy banning all drinks except water at Rowdown Primary School in New Addington, south London, citing long-term health benefits. Some parents disagreed, arguing that their children dislike water and feel the rule is too restrictive. The opposition has launched a campaign to change the policy, claiming it infringes on parental rights to choose what their children drink. The school acknowledges the concerns but stands by the decision to enforce the water-only rule for the children's long-term health. The controversy follows similar incidents at other schools. Some experts advocate for healthier drink options in schools, regarding fruit juice as too sugary to be consumed daily but not daily.

Boxer Paul Smith has secured a highly challenging fight against Andre Ward in Oakland, California on June 20th. This fight is not for Ward's WBA super-middleweight world title, but represents a significant opportunity for Smith who previously failed in challenges for Arthur Abraham's WBO belt. Smith, who outclassed Carl Froch in 2011, is enthusiastic about the match, stating he's eager to test himself against a renowned boxer like Ward. Ward, who's had only one fight in nearly three years, expressed his excitement about returning to the ring and assured fans that he'll put up a strong defense against Smith.

Angela Merkel and her husband, Joachim Sauer, are spending their annual Easter holiday in Italy at the five-star Miramare Spa Hotel on Ischia. Due to the cooler weather, Merkel has reportedly been avoiding the pool and lounges, instead focusing on Pilates classes and vegetarian meals. Her husband, a professor of theoretical chemistry, typically stays out of the limelight and did not attend Merkel's inauguration in 2005. Hotel prices start at £160 per night but can go up to £280 for some suites.

Ander Herrera, a midfielder for Manchester United, scored a brace against Aston Villa with his eyes closed, adding to his history of scoring without looking at the ball or the opposition's net. Louis van Gaal praised Herrera's shooting technique but emphasized the need for more composure and control in his shots. Despite his closing-eyes approach, Herrera has contributed numerous goals to Manchester United's season.

A 23-month-old girl died tragically in North Las Vegas after her father unknowingly hit her with a pickup truck in the driveway. The incident, deemed an accident, occurred Thursday morning, with the toddler set to turn two this weekend. The names of the family members and the father involved have not been publicly disclosed.

The University of Connecticut's baseball team has welcomed a new member, 5-year-old Grayson Hand who is battling leukemia, through the help of Team IMPACT. Grayson, who now has his own locker with the team, will be able to attend games and practices. His 7-year-old sister, Sophie, was named an honorary cheerleader. Father Nate Hand described the partnership as a physical representation of the outpouring of emotional support they've received.

A passenger on a London Midland train from Lichfield Trent Valley to Longbridge discovered excrement in a newspaper on the floor, causing a severe delay due to the train's cancellation and subsequent cleaning. The incident, described as an act of vandalism, resulted in London Midland providing CCTV images of the suspect to the police for investigation. The British Transport Police have no formal record of a complaint regarding this incident, though a similar incident involving a foul odor on a British Airways flight occurred last month.

James Rodriguez, the Real Madrid midfielder, is being lauded by Spanish newspaper Marca for his exceptional form since joining from Monaco. Rodriguez's presence has significantly improved the team's performance, with Real Madrid winning 80% of their games when he's on the field compared to just 58% without him. Marca has dubbed the Colombian as 'the jewel in Real Madrid's crown' and credits him with influencing 13 goals and 12 assists this season. Rodriguez's success also includes living up to his £60 million price tag and earning praise for his performances in the No. 10 role.

Meanwhile, AS is covering Real Madrid's appeal against Cristiano Ronaldo's yellow card for diving in a match against Rayo Vallecano. The competition and appeals committee is scheduled to meet on Friday to discuss the matter.

In other Italian news, La Gazzetta dello Sport reports that Roberto Mancini, the former Manchester City manager, has plans for a summer revolution at Inter Milan. The list of potential new signings includes Yaya Toure, Filipe Luis,

A Florida man, Kenneth Crowder, was arrested in Melbourne after running naked through a neighborhood, claiming to be God, and engaging in unspecified lewd behavior on a tree. He was later identified as being under the influence of Flakka, a designer drug said to be stronger than crystal meth. The incident resulted in charges of battery on a law-enforcement officer, resisting with violence, and assault with a deadly weapon. Flakka, also known as $5 insanity, is known for its potent psychoactive effects and increased prevalence in Florida, with more than 670 occurrences in 2014 compared to zero in 2010.

A Russian Premier League match between Arsenal Tula and Torpedo Moscow was suspended for seven minutes due to fighting caused by Torpedo fans breaking down barriers, attempting to enter the East Stand where women and children were sitting, and throwing chairs at law enforcement officers and stewards. The incident led to an on-field brawl and fights on the running track. Referees temporarily halted the match, and after order was restored, Torpedo won 3-1. Due to the fans' repeated violent behavior, the team is expected to face severe punishment, including potential match suspensions. Torpedo has been previously punished for racist behavior of its supporters.

High school girls in Huizhou, China are undergoing intense military-style knife fighting training under the instruction of ex-special forces soldier Inspector Tan. The training, which includes eight key movements and shouting phrases like "kill, stab, slash, jab," is designed to teach the girls how to defend themselves using any sharp object, such as chopsticks. Although the knives used in training have retractable plastic blades and pose no danger, the school purchased 250 of them for all female students, with the intent of teaching self-defense skills to help students identify and avoid dangerous situations. The five-day training session has gained popularity due to the learning of the latest self-defense techniques.

AP McCoy, champion jockey since 1997, has declared his intent to retire immediately if his mount Shutthefrontdoor wins the Grand National on Saturday. Shutthefrontdoor, trained by Jonjo O'Neill, has received an influx of emotional support and is a popular choice among casual punters. McCoy seeks a fairytale end to his illustrious career, having won the race once before in 2010 on Don't Push It. He acknowledges the unpredictability of jump racing but remains optimistic about his chances. He also expressed gratitude for the increased interest in racing resulting from his retirement announcement.

Tennis player John Isner, a 6-foot-10 American, advanced to the Miami Open semifinals by defeating Kei Nishikori 6-4, 6-3. Isner, known for his hard serving, had not made it this far in Miami since 2011. In the semifinals, he will play either Novak Djokovic or David Ferrer. Meanwhile, Andy Murray will face Tomas Berdych in another semi final, rekindling a rivalry that started during their Australian Open semi-final match earlier this year. Murray's former coach Jez Green and Berdych's assistant coach Dani Vallverdu previously worked together before joining Murray and Berdych's teams, respectively. Kim Sears, Murray's wife, was reported to have expressed anger toward Berdych during the Australian Open.

German football legend Franz Beckenbauer criticized Bayern Munich's performance in their Champions League quarter-final defeat against Porto, labeling it as if the players had taken "sleeping pills." He specifically accused defender Dante of playing poorly, likening his performance to wearing "ski boots." Despite these harsh words, Beckenbauer acknowledged that Bayern Munich still has a chance to advance to the semi-finals, but would need to significantly improve their performance.

A 21-year-old man, Arnold Quintero from San Antonio, Texas, has been arrested on charges including aggravated sexual assault and sex performed by a child under 14, following allegations of imprisoning, assaulting, and sexually assaulting a 13-year-old girl. The girl claimed she was held captive in a 'trap house' between January 21 and February 8, and suffered physical and sexual abuse during this time, including being burned with a lighter. The Bexar County Sheriff’s Office Criminal Investigations Division interviewed the girl last month, and she identified Quintero in a photographic lineup.

World No 1 Michael van Gerwen had a mixed night in Week 12 of the Betway Premier League, beating James Wade 7-0 but losing to Gary Anderson 7-5 during their match-up. Anderson, world champion, had also experienced atypical performances, winning against Van Gerwen and losing to Stephen Bunting in the opening match. Other notable results included Raymond van Barneveld beating Dave Chisnall and Phil Taylor drawing with Adrian Lewis.

In summary, British training consultant Jay Rutland, 34, and wife Tamara Ecclestone, a billionaire heiress, have a lavish lifestyle despite Jay's consulting firm, Brigante Business Developments, having a modest profit of £3,378 for the year to July 2014. Rutland's career in the City of London ended in disgrace due to market abuse allegations in 2012, and he has faced personal troubles, including a mugging incident where he was robbed of expensive watches. The couple, despite these challenges, are reportedly worth billions, owning a series of high-end vehicles, and recently celebrated their daughter Sophia's first birthday in style with an extravagant farmyard-themed party.

A leukaemia patient, Jia Binhui, aged 25, resides in Yunlong County, China, and due to financial constraints, cannot afford hospital treatment. In an attempt to combat the disease, Jia has constructed a makeshift fire-heated contraption in his backyard, which he believes, based on expert advice, will reach a temperature exceeding 42 degrees Celsius, sufficient to kill cancer cells. Despite his dire situation, Jia found resilience in marrying his long-term partner last month and remains optimistic about improving his condition using this unconventional treatment.

Quees Park Rangers midfielder Leroy Fer, who has been sidelined with a knee injury since February, could be rushed back into action to aid the team's relegation battle. Manager Chris Ramsey has expressed hope that Fer will be available for the London derby against West Ham on Saturday. However, Ramsey acknowledges that the club is taking a risk with Fer's health, as he has struggled with form and fitness since joining from Norwich in the summer. Additionally, QPR has several key players returning from injuries, including defender Richard Dunne and Korean left-back Yun Suk-Young, although Rio Ferdinand remains unavailable.

1. In the Scheldeprijs race on Wednesday, Team Sky riders Sir Bradley Wiggins and Geraint Thomas managed to avoid a major crash, while their teammate Elia Viviani wasn't so fortunate and was involved in a crash that sent around 50 riders to the ground.

2. Elia Viviani, who was competing for a sprint finish, sustained injuries to his arm and ribs and was taken to hospital for x-rays.

3. The crash occurred just before the expected sprint finish, and the winner was Katusha's Alexander Kristoff, with only 14 riders contesting the sprint. Team Sky remained optimistic about their performance, with Wiggins having a penultimate outing for the team before the Paris-Roubaix on Sunday.

Aston Villa players received messages of encouragement from fans in their dressing room before the FA Cup semi-final against Liverpool. Jack Grealish thanked fans on Twitter, sharing a message from supporter Mike Shenaniganz Cope that read, "You have to put up with the rain to see the rainbow! Three seasons of rain boys, time to find the end of that rainbow and prove we're the pride of the Midlands!" Aston Villa coach Tim Sherwood included Grealish in the starting lineup, and goalkeeper Brad Guzan also shared the contents of his inspiring fan-sent message.

A 12-year-old named Hanghang in central China was seriously injured when his old phone exploded while charging, exposing part of his jawbone and embedding fragments in his arms and legs. Doctors believe the explosion was likely caused by improper charging, leading to overheating and a sudden discharge of current. Hanghang is currently being treated in a hospital and is expected to undergo several operations to repair the damage. To prevent similar accidents, experts advise against using the phone while charging, removing the electric supply when the battery is fully charged, and replacing swollen batteries immediately.

Mike Rowe, known for his television series "Somebody's Gotta Do It," features Chad Pregracke, the founder of Living Lands & Waters, who is recognized for his efforts to clean up U.S. rivers. Pregracke and his volunteers have collected 8.4 million pounds of trash since 1998, earning him the 2013 CNN Hero of the Year Award. He operates on a barge that serves as a home, office, and dumpster, made from a recycled strip club, with a goal to remove an additional 500,000 pounds of trash in 2015. To get involved and help achieve this goal, visit LivingLandsAndWaters.org.

The abandoned ghost town of Balestrino, dating back to the 11th century, was once home to 800 inhabitants but was left uninhabited due to seismic instability, with significant damage caused by the earthquake in 1887. Today, the crumbling structures and castle on the hill give a haunting eeriness to the town, earning it the reputation as Italy's most famous abandoned location, often rumored to be haunted. A recently shot drone footage captures the town's desolate beauty, highlighting the grandeur of the castle and the darkness of the empty, abandoned buildings.

The article describes a Star Wars event where director J.J. Abrams and the cast of Episode VII - The Force Awakens presented the trailer and audience reactions were positive. Key takeaways from the event include: Han Solo and Chewbacca flying the Millennium Falcon, a new planet called Jakku replacing Tatooine as a main location, hints of Luke and Leia's involvement without their physical presence, less CGI usage compared to the prequels, and the presence of a crashed Star Destroyer and Vader's charred helmet in the trailer.

Rob Ford, the former Toronto Mayor, has announced that he will undergo surgery to remove a cancerous tumor in his abdomen on May 11. He has shared that the tumor, initially diagnosed as malignant liposarcoma, has been significantly shrunk through chemotherapy and radiation. Ford hopes for a recovery by September and a return to work as a councilor.

A South African university has removed the statue of British colonialist Cecil Rhodes following weeks of protests by students who consider his legacy symbols of racism and supremacy. The statue was taken down after a heritage authority granted permission. Opposing this action are some protesters who see the statue as an important part of the country's history and argue that removing it equates to erasing history. Students who led the campaign view the statue's removal as a step towards creating an Afrocentric university that appreciates African thought.

Michael Phelps, the 18-time Olympic gold medalist, made a victorious return to competitive swimming after a six-month suspension for a drink driving conviction. He won the 100 meters butterfly event at the Arena Pro Swim Series in Arizona, edging out Ryan Lochte. Despite missing the World Championships in Kazan, Russia this summer, Phelps intends to compete at the 2016 Olympics in Rio de Janeiro.

A New York woman was found hanging from a third-floor fire escape of her apartment building in Crown Heights on Sunday morning. The incident left witnesses traumatized, with one individual initially suspecting it was a Halloween prank. The woman's identity has not been release pending notifying her family, and neighbors described her as a friendly and social individual who struggled with mental health issues. The National Suicide Prevention Lifeline number (1-800-273-8255) is provided for confidential help.

1. Lyon and Saint-Etienne played a 2-2 draw in the Rhone Valley derby, with Lyon moving back to the top of Ligue 1 due to the result. Clinton N'Jie and Christophe Jallet scored for Lyon, with Romain Hamouma getting a goal for Saint-Etienne.

2. Lille beat Bordeaux 2-0 at home, with Nolan Roux and Adama Traore getting the goals. This was Lille's sixth win in seven games, and they are now just four points behind Bordeaux, who they are still chasing in the race for fourth place.

3. Montpellier earned a 1-0 victory over Caen, with Brazilian defender Hilton scoring the only goal of the game. The win moved Montpellier up to seventh in the Ligue 1 standings, while Caen remain in 13th after a poor run of form.

Arsene Wenger expresses surprise over Hector Bellerin and Francis Coquelin's significant contributions to Arsenal's late league push, as he initially considered Coquelin not a first-choice player and Bellerin was loaned out last year without much expectation. Bellerin, aged 20, impressed against Liverpool, scoring a crucial goal and handling Raheem Sterling effectively, demonstrating his defensive and attacking potential. Despite a potential booking incident, Wenger acknowledged Bellerin's mental strength, and credited his defense and forward play. The Arsenal boss admitted he considered Coquelin expendable, having sent him on loan to Charlton before Christmas.

Fox is developing a two-hour remake of "The Rocky Horror Picture Show," directed by Kenneth Ortega, to celebrate the film's 40th anniversary. The remake, titled "The Rocky Horror Picture Show Event," is being executive-produced by Gail Berman and Lou Adler, who produced the original film. The production is by Fox 21 Television Studios and The Jackal Group.
