This isn't the first attempt to adapt the cult classic, as a previous Fox project planned for the 30th anniversary never came to fruition. The air date for the remake is currently unknown.

Roman football club AS Roma has been ordered to partially close their stadium for an upcoming game after offensive banners were displayed during their match against Napoli, mocking the mother of a Napoli supporter who was killed in violent clashes last year. The banners caused outrage, and the Serie A disciplinary tribunal described them as "provocatively insulting." AS Roma's stadium will be part-closed for the league match with Atalanta on April 19 due to the sanction. Club president James Pallotta has condemned the fans' actions and expressed sympathy towards the late fan's mother, Antonella Leardi, who said she was hurt by the words on the banners.

Ellen White, the Notts County footballer, had a memorable night as she scored against her former club Arsenal in the Women's Super League. The goal came from a well-executed free kick in the 26th minute that was somewhat hindered by confusion among the Arsenal defenders. White spun on the edge of the box and fired the ball into the corner, turning a special moment into a 1-1 draw. Despite missing a penalty that could have made it 2-0, White's historic goal remained a significant achievement. Arsenal salvaged a point late in the game when Chioma Ubogagu scored her debut goal for the club.

Arsene Wenger acknowledges discussions about signing Eden Hazard from Lille in 2012, but could not afford him due to financial constraints, with Chelsea eventually securing him for £32million. Wenger admits that Hazard's outstanding season makes him a frontrunner for Player of the Year, but believes Alexis Sanchez, also in the running, may still have a chance, given Sanchez is in his first season at Arsenal. Wenger praises Hazard for improved maturity, better final ball, stronger on-pitch personality, and ability to turn games in tight situations, making him a sign of top quality.

Stephen Akers-Belcher, the former mayor of Hartlepool, was dismissed from his care manager role with Newcastle City Council for gross misconduct after he was pictured attending HMS Warrior during a paid leave supposedly taken for compassionate reasons. The photos revealed Akers-Belcher was 323 miles away from his jurisdiction. Akers-Belcher had initially claimed he was attending a funeral during the time in question, but his story was disputed when evidence showed he was at HMS Warrior instead. Akers-Belcher maintains he did nothing wrong, but the council denies his dismissal had anything to do with whistleblowing and contends the allegations he made were made after their investigation into his conduct began.

A highly experienced general practitioner, Doctor John Parker, who had been working at an Australian-run Ebola treatment clinic in Sierra Leone since November, was taken to Westmead Hospital in Sydney for testing after exhibiting flu-like symptoms. tests conducted by the hospital's lab have since returned negative for Ebola, and NSW Health confirmed no further testing is required at this stage. Dr Parker's employer, Aspen Medical, confirmed he had followed protocol and notified authorities as a precaution, as his slight increase in temperature occurred after returning from Sierra Leone, where over 10,000 people have died from the Ebola virus, according to the World Health Organization.

A 9-year-old England-based football prodigy, Frankie Franz, mimicked Barcelona's Martin Montoya by scoring a basketball-style goal from 27 yards into a backyard basketball hoop, twice. After watching a viral video of Montoya making the trick shot at Barcelona's training ground, Frankie, an academy player at Dagenham and Redbridge FC, successfully replicated the feat in his garden. His mother, amazed by the accomplishment, noted that Frankie is very skilled at football and aspires to play for Real Madrid or Barcelona in the future.

The Wisden–MCC Cricket Photograph of the Year 2014 short-list includes a variety of breathtaking shots showcasing the global reach of cricket. The winning image captures Dwayne Bravo taking a spectacular catch for the West Indies during the ICC World Twenty20 competition in Bangladesh. The list includes pictures of ordinary players, such as children on a rubbish tip in Bangladesh and club players in Kent, as well as extraordinary moments like a game of cricket on Mount Kilimanjaro's summit crater. The competition's runner-up image features England's Joe Russell making an athletic but unsuccessful attempt at a catch.

A New Jersey judge has ruled in favor of a mother who took her 11-year-old daughter to a Pink concert, dismissing the father's claims of "abusing parental discretion." The judge found the mother did not exceed reasonable judgment in allowing the child to attend the show, as the girl was "dying to go" and the performance was deemed age-appropriate after the mother researched clips on YouTube. The judge also highlighted Pink's music as containing messages suitable for adolescents, despite some suggestive elements.

1. Salcombe, a coastal town in Devon, has become the most expensive place in the UK to buy property, with an average cost of £671,759, surpassing London's average of £638,217. This also makes Salcombe more expensive than some of the UK's other expensive cities, such as Oxford, Bath, and Edinburgh.

2. The cost of waterfront properties in Salcombe is particularly high, with some properties costing up to £2 million, making it more expensive than some of London's priciest areas like Notting Hill, Regent's Park, and Hampstead Heath.

3. Despite its high property prices, Salcombe, known as 'Chelsea-on-Sea', is a popular destination for UK travellers due to its yachting and sailing paradise, fresh seafood, and stunning beaches. For those interested in experiencing the millionaire lifestyle on a budget, the Salcombe Harbour Hotel & Spa offers waterfront rooms starting from £425 this summer season.

Celtic has criticized the Scottish Football Association (SFA) for setting prices too high for tickets to their Scottish Cup semi-final against Inverness, with Celtic fans complaining about ticket prices in the North stand being set at £23, while the East stand is £15 for adults and £5 for concessions. The SFA maintains that ticket prices have remained the same for the past four years and that revenue from the semi-finals is split evenly among the participating teams. Meanwhile, Celtic's manager Ronny Deila is preparing his team for their Scottish Premiership League clash with St. Mirren on Friday.

A pupil, Rebecca Rice, brought her 11-year-old pet Labrador, Holly, into a GCSE French oral exam at Bodmin College in Cornwall due to her severe nerves. The school allowed this exceptional measure upon teacher Lorette Esteve's advice, as Rebecca found comfort in the presence of Holly. This relaxation tactic was part of the school's efforts to reduce stress during the exam period, which also included bringing comfort items like drinks, lucky key rings, or a friend into the exam room.

Anders Lindegaard, the goalkeeper for Manchester United, is enjoying his life off the pitch, spending time with his wife, Swedish model Misse Beqiri, whom he married last year in a beach wedding in Mauritius. The couple have a son together and Lindegaard often shares photos with Beqiri on his Instagram page. Despite difficulties in securing regular playing time at Manchester United, Lindegaard is attracting attention for his personal life rather than his performance on the pitch. He has been linked with a move to FC Midtjylland but could not reach an agreement with the club.

Manchester United goalkeepers David de Gea and Victor Valdes took a break from their professional duties and visited a theme park on Tuesday, enjoying a relaxing day out amidst United's impressive winning streak in the Premier League. United have improved their position in the league, challenging Arsenal for second place after struggling earlier in the season. However, the future of both Valdes and De Gea at Old Trafford is uncertain, leaving their summer plans in doubt.

A piano teacher, John Goodwin, 75, shot himself outside a New Hampshire courthouse while jurors were deliberating on charges of aggravated felonious sexual assault. Goodwin, who pleaded not guilty, had been awaiting a jury's verdict for allegedly sexually assaulting an underage student, now 24, who testified he didn't come forward until 2013 due to embarrassment. His health status is currently unknown following the self-inflicted gunshot wound. The New Hampshire Attorney General's Office is expected to release more information about the incident.

Amazon has removed a computer game titled "Rescue the Anorexia Girl" from its platform due to backlash. The game, which was marketed by SmartTouch media and available on Amazon and Android, invited players to throw food at a cartoon girl character who is depicted as having anorexia. The game's instructions promoted the idea that players could save the character from her illness. Social media users have criticized the game for further stigmatizing people with eating disorders and for promoting harmful stereotypes.

Researchers, notably the Green Brain Project team, aim to recreate the cognitive abilities of European Honeybees to power drones. The focus is on creating a robot that thinks, senses, and acts like the honeybee. Although they've achieved cloning the part of the bee's brain responsible for sight, they're currently developing more complex functions. Experimental tests with quadcopters and a ground robot are ongoing at the University of Sheffield. The ultimate goals are to use these machines for tasks such as pollinating crops or aiding in search and rescue missions.

A newly-wed couple, both employees of Air Malta, embarked on a romantic flight over the Mediterranean shortly after their wedding at Malta's international airport. The Airbus A319 flight took an unusual heart-shaped route, with stops in Malta and at Sicily's Mount Etna, for a sight-seeing tour with family and friends. While some viewers saw it as a creative training exercise, Air Malta confirmed it was a celebratory flight for the married couple.

A giraffe named Melvin was gored to death by an eland antelope at Kristiansand Zoo in Norway. The attack occurred when Melvin had his head stuck in a fence, and around 30 people, including many children, were witnesses to the incident. Veterinary attempts to save Melvin were unsuccessful. The cause of the unprovoked attack remains unclear.

A restaurant in Leuven, Belgium, has been criticized as having the 'stingiest boss in Europe' after charging a mother 36p to warm up her baby's feeding bottle, leading to outrage on social media. Mum Gitte Denteneer received a bill for about £20, including an omelette, two cappuccinos, and two desserts, with the bottle-warming fee adding 50 cents. The restaurant chain later stated that the customer had been explicitly told that this service was charged.

North Korea's cargo ship, the Mu Du Bong, was detained by Mexico in July after it ran aground, following allegations that its owning company, North Korea's Ocean Maritime Management, has repeatedly skirted UN sanctions. Mexico defended its actions, claiming they followed international obligations as a responsible UN member state. Mexico's U.N. mission stated that the 33 North Korean crew members are currently in a hotel in Tuxpan, free to visit the ship and will soon be sent back to North Korea. This situation contrasts with the 2013 detainment of another North Korean ship, the Chong Chon Gang, by Panama, which found undeclared weaponry on board.

Prime Minister David Cameron plans to offer 600,000 additional free childcare places each year, aiming to reduce costs as a barrier to employment, particularly for second earners. The initiative is expected to cost £350 million and will provide 30 hours of childcare weekly for eligible three- and four-year-olds, saving working families up to £5,000 annually. The Conservatives argue that this policy fosters a socially compassionate environment by creating opportunities for employment, thereby promoting a society that rewards hard work and reducing poverty through work.

Manchester City's young team secured a 5-1 aggregate victory over Leicester City in the Youth Cup, with goals from Isaac Buckley and Brandon Barker in the final minutes of the match at King Power Stadium. Earlier, Layton Ndukwu scored a penalty to give Leicester some hope, but City held on to advance to the final against Chelsea, with the first leg scheduled for April 20 at the City Football Academy Stadium, followed by the second leg at Stamford Bridge on April 27.

Russian President Vladimir Putin downplayed the effects of Western sanctions on his country during an annual Q&A session, stating they were more about restraining Russia's development rather than specifically targeting Ukraine and Crimea. He defended the decision to lift sanctions on the sale of a sophisticated air defense system to Iran, claiming it was a move to encourage Iranian partners in relation to the preliminary deal concerning Iran's nuclear program. Putin's annual Q&A session is a highly controlled event where he primarily speaks to the public and international audience, with a record-breaking session lasting over four hours in 2013. Over 2.4 million questions were submitted for this year's session, although critics argue the event is more a choreographed opportunity for Putin to address the public rather than an interactive forum for questions and answers.

Aston Villa manager Tim Sherwood is set to assess midfielder Gary Gardner during pre-season, as the 22-year-old, who had a successful loan stint at Nottingham Forest, returns to the club after impressing in a game Sherwood attended. Born in Solihull, Gardner joined Villa's academy at seven, and despite suffering serious knee injuries, he expressed his desire to make an impact at the club following a new contract last year. If opportunities don't materialize at Villa, Gardner stated that Nottingham Forest would be his preferred loan destination again.

A stampede occurred at a nightclub in Santiago, Chile, during a British punk band's performance, resulting in three fatalities and over a dozen injuries. The incident transpired when a large group attempted to force entry into the Tsunami nightclub to see the British Crust Punk band Doom. Police confirmed that a structural collapse within the building due to the crush caused the deaths and injuries. The identities of the deceased have not been officially disclosed, and seven people were reported critically injured, with several arrests made in relation to the tragedy. The band Doom is known for their Crust Punk genre and tracks such as Anti-Social and Raining Napalm.

Bayern Munich advanced to the semi-final of the German Cup after a 5-3 penalty shoot-out victory against Bayer Leverkusen, but Pep Guardiola expressed concern about his team's scoring form and the absence of Franck Ribery and Arjen Robben. Ribery is currently sidelined with an ankle injury, while Robben is out until May with a stomach muscle tear. Guardiola believes his team struggles in one-on-one situations without these two key players, and they will aim to adapt when they host Eintracht Frankfurt in their next Bundesliga match. The one goal scored by Bayern in their last three matches came from Robert Lewandowski in a 1-0 win against Borussia Dortmund, and they will face each other again in the German Cup semi-final.

Derry Mathews' world title challenge is currently in limbo due to Richard Abril's repeated withdrawal from their fight for the WBA lightweight belt, which was scheduled for April 18 in Liverpool. Mathews may still contend for the title in Liverpool if the WBA decides to strip Abril of his belt. Recent events follow Mathews' impressive fifth-round knockout against Gyorgy Mezei Jnr on March 6. Abril had previously withdrawn ahead of their initial fight date on March 6 and has fought infrequently since 2012. Mathews expressed disappointment that Abril did not want to fight, claiming that his team will secure a suitable replacement for the title fight.

1. An English Bulldog named Hazel demonstrates exuberant curiosity by attempting to conquer a washing basket, resulting in humorous mishaps like toppling the basket and tumbling out inside it.
2. The video captures various moments of Hazel exploring her environment, including playing on a skateboard, observing her reflection, and trying on various collars.
3. These playful antics are often shared on Hazel's dedicated YouTube and Instagram channels, showcasing her endearing and mischievous nature.

Catholic bishops in the U.S. have criticized the BBC drama "Wolf Hall," currently airing for the first time, for its negative portrayal of historical figures, particularly Thomas Cromwell and Thomas More. The series, which stars Damian Lewis and Anton Lesser, is observed as advancing an anti-Catholic perspective and misrepresenting characters, according to the Catholic News Service. This criticism follows similar critiques emanating from the U.K. Upon its U.S. premiere, the drama was generally anticipated as an engaging British import, with Homeland actor Damian Lewis playing King Henry VIII. However, one U.S. publication, The Washington Post, flagged potential distortions of historical facts within the series as an indication of ideological bias. Despite the controversy, "Wolf Hall" was BBC2's most-watched drama since 2002, averaging 4.4 million viewers during its six-week run.

Today, victims of the 2009 Fort Hood shooting are set to receive Purple Heart medals, but some, like Staff Sergeant Shawn Manning, claim they have been denied crucial financial support. Manning was shot six times in the attack, but the Army has rejected his claims that his injuries were sustained in the line of duty, thereby denying him benefits under the 2015 National Defense Authorization Act. Notably, the attack was initially classified as workplace violence, but it was subsequently acknowledged as an act of terrorism inspired by a foreign terrorist group. The Army has stated that it will make a final decision regarding Manning's case and allow him a formal hearing. It is known that Major Nidal Hasan, the perpetrator of the attack, had prior communications with Anwar al-Awlaki, an al-Qaeda spokesperson, who subsequently praised Hasan's actions.

John Carver, the head coach of Newcastle United, faces a challenging job due to fans' discontent with the club's management under Mike Ashley, exacerbated by recent poor performances. The fans are planning a boycott of the upcoming match against Tottenham Hotspur in protest against Ashley's perceived lack of investment and ambition, as the club has reported record profits and has £34 million in a bank account. Despite the mounting pressure, Carver appeals for fan support, acknowledging their concerns yet emphasizing the need for unity during difficult times.

Jordan Spieth, 21, won the 2015 Masters tournament at Augusta, becoming the first player to reach 19 under par in the event. He maintained a four-shot advantage throughout the final day, securing his victory with a final round of 70. Having finished second at the Masters in 2014, Spieth's win marks a significant accomplishment in his young career. Born in Dallas, Texas, Spieth gained attention as a teenager, winning two US Junior Amateur titles and making the cut at a PGA event at the age of 17. He turned professional in 2012, winning the PGA Tour Rookie of the Year award, and has since amassed multiple victories and made a name for himself as one of golf's brightest young stars off the course as well, recently purchasing a mansion in his hometown.

Beatrice Tollman, founder of a luxury hotel chain, donated £20,000 to the Conservative Party in support of their General Election campaign, but was previously charged with conspiracy to evade tax charges that were later dismissed. Her husband, Stanley Tollman, pleaded guilty to tax evasion in 2008, and was required to repay over $100 million. The Tollmans' son also pleaded guilty to tax evasion. These tax-related offenses, along with David Cameron's observed disapproval of tax evasion, may cause embarrassment for the Conservative Party, especially as they have committed to crack down on tax avoidance in their manifesto. A Conservative spokesperson stated that they will be returning any donations from the Tollmans in light of these findings.

A 23-year-old marketing coordinator named Poppy Smart complained to police after experiencing daily sexual harassment in the form of wolf-whistling from builders during her walk to work in Worcester city centre. The whistling, which included lewd comments and a near confrontation, escalated to the point where she felt intimidated and her anxiety worsened. After a month of such behavior, she contacted both the police and the construction company, comparing the wolf-whistling to racial discrimination. The builders were working on the expansion of the Bolero restaurant, and since her complaint, she has not encountered them again. Although wolf-whistling is not a specific offense, it has been deemed a possible incident of anti-social behavior, and the construction company has been asked to address the issue. The End Violence Against Women Coalition considers wolf-whistling to be a form of everyday sexism that should be discouraged.

A UK teenager named Lily Sharp played a prank on her mother by faking her own kidnapping, referencing the film "Taken" in her initial text. The prank was elaborate, with Lily convincing her mother that a stranger had entered the home and taken her phone. The broke suspense by revealing it was a joke, but her mother was not amused. Despite the reaction, the prank received significant attention on Twitter.

On March 17, 2015, in the first one-day international in Dhaka, Bangladesh defeated Pakistan by 79 runs, advancing to the World Cup quarterfinals. Centuries from Tamim Iqbal (132) and Mushfiqur Rahim (106) powered Bangladesh to 329/6, while Pakistan struggled to 250/9 in response. The second ODI is scheduled for Sunday in Mirpur. During the match, Iqbal and Rahim rebuilt Bangladesh's wobbly innings with a partnership of 178 runs, while Pakistan's batting lineup consistently fell short, with only Azhar Ali (72) reaching significant score. Sunny and Ahmed took three wickets each for Bangladesh, with Pakistan ultimately unable to meet the target score, losing by 79 runs.

Todd Kincannon, a 33-year-old Columbia attorney and former South Carolina Republican Party executive director, has been arrested and charged with criminal domestic violence following an incident involving his wife, Ashley Griffith, last month. The arrest warrant alleges that Kincannon grabbed Griffith's arm during an argument, preventing her from exiting the vehicle, and threatened to kill her, himself, and her family. Additional evidence, including forty-eight hours of audio recordings and photographic evidence, suggests a pattern of verbal abuse towards Griffith. Kincannon has garnered a reputation for sending inflammatory tweets, including a tweet about Janay Palmer in the NFL scandal that was widely perceived as racist and sexist. Since his arrest, Kincannon has deleted his Twitter account.

Jordan Spieth, fresh from winning the Masters and breaking Tiger Woods' record, is participating in the RBC Heritage Classic this week despite a busy media schedule. He arrives having completed 26 appearances and interviews in 25 hours. Spieth, aiming to surpass Rory McIlroy as the world's top-ranked golfer, views the tournament as an opportunity to advance his goal. Despite a quick turnaround, Spieth has had success at the venue, finishing ninth in 2013 and 12th last year. He finds the tournament meaningful, as it helped his confidence and boosted his standing on the PGA Tour. Spieth has risen to the top of the FedEx Cup standings, making him the youngest player ever to lead in this category. Despite the media attention, Spieth remains focused on his quest for golfing excellence.

Samantha Cameron, a former British Prime Minister's wife, showcased her appreciation for the alternative band Poliça, known for their psychedelic rock and violent, feminist-inspired imagery. The band's album cover, titled "Shulamith" and featuring a graphic image of a blood-soaked woman, is named after Shulamith Firestone, a radical feminist who wrote about the liberation of women from men and the abolition of childbirth. Samantha, despite her aristocratic background, has expressed a love for indie music and Radio 6 Music.

The federal government plans to impose a 10% GST on digital movie and music downloads from streaming services like Netflix and Apple, aiming to increase revenue. This may also affect consumers purchasing online products from overseas up to $1,000, affecting companies such as Google, Microsoft, Amazon, and eBay. However, consumer advocacy group Choice suggests that the government should focus on reducing domestic costs for TV shows, music, and movies, and improving accessibility instead. Netflix and other companies have indicated they would adjust their prices in response to new laws and regulations. Consumers are advised that they might be able to avoid the tax by concealing their location through virtual private networks.

ESPN's Stephen A. Smith is facing criticism for his stance on boxer Floyd Mayweather Jr., who has a history of domestic violence convictions. Smith argued that Mayweather's boxing career should be considered separately from his violent history, and when co-host Cari Champion disagreed, Smith suggested that her opinion was a result of her being a woman. This controversy is not new for Smith, as he previously faced backlash for victim-blaming in a 2014 discussion about the Ray Rice scandal.

A 12-year-old boy named Mahendra Ahirwar from Madhya Pradesh, India, suffers from a rare condition that causes his head to hang at a 180-degree angle, limiting his ability to stand, walk, eat, or use the toilet independently. His parents, who are laborers, have consulted more than 50 doctors across India but his condition remains undiagnosed. Despite their efforts, his mother Sumitra Ahirwar has expressed her desperation, stating that she would rather see him dead than continue to suffer. Community members, however, blame Mahendra's condition on his father's past sins. The family has no hope for a diagnosis or treatment and struggles to care for him as he grows older.

The World Happiness Report 2015 revealed Switzerland as the world's happiest nation, due to factors including healthy GDP figures, strong social bonds, and increasing life expectancy. Iceland, known for its beautiful scenery and cultural history, moved up to the second spot on the list. The least happy countries include those embroiled in war and extreme poverty, with Syria, Burundi, and Togo at the bottom. Surprisingly, Palestine ranked below the midway point. The study analyzed nations based on factors contributing to citizen satisfaction rather than wealth alone, with European nations, especially those in Scandinavia, dominating the top 10. Notably, Greece experienced the fastest decline due to economic difficulties.

The article previews the upcoming Premier League match between Burnley and Arsenal at Turf Moor, providing team news, provisional squads, betting odds, and Opta stats. Burnley's Matt Taylor could potentially return from a long-term achilles injury and Ross Wallace and Steven Reid might also feature. Key players for Arsenal, including Laurent Koscielny and Santi Cazorla, are aiming to pass fitness tests. Both teams have specific statistical trends; Burnley have let in many goals in their recent matches against Arsenal, while Arsenal have won seven consecutive league games. The match kicks off on Saturday at 5:30pm and can be viewed on Sky Sports 1.

Ahead of the Premier League match between Tottenham and Aston Villa, Sportsmail provides team news, squads, betting odds, and Opta stats. Tottenham will be missing Kyle Walker and Hugo Lloris, with Vertonghen also a doubt. Aston Villa is set to miss a key trio including Alan Hutton and Ashley Westwood, with Carles Gil and Libor Kozak remaining sidelined. Betting odds favor Tottenham with 4/7 odds, while accidentally conceding multiple first-half goals at White Hart Lane is a notable statistic. Key players in focus include Harry Kane for Tottenham and Christian Benteke for Aston Villa.

The article previews the Premier League match between Liverpool and Newcastle United at Anfield, providing team news, provisional squads, betting odds, and Opta stats. Liverpool defender Mamadou Sakho is out due to a hamstring injury, but Emre Can returns from suspension. Daniel Sturridge and Mario Balotelli may also feature. Newcastle defender Daryl Janmaat is expected to play despite an injury scare. Papiss Cisse is suspended, while Rolando Aarons and Siem de Jong remain unavailable. Liverpool are the favorites with odds of 4/11, and Newcastle's last clean sheet against them was in 1993-94. The game has a history of high-scoring encounters, with 130 goals in total, and Newcastle have been sent off in five of the last five meetings. Jordan Henderson has scored in four of his last five Premier League appearances for Liverpool, while Ayoze Perez scored the only goal when the teams met in November. Liverpool have not scored as many goals at this stage this season as they had at the same point last season.

Nick Clegg, the Liberal Democrat leader, has been accused of deflecting responsibility for his party's dismal poll ratings, citing various reasons for embittered former supporters' defection since 2010. In an interview, he identified protest voters, public sector workers, and individuals unwilling to take responsibility as primary causes of lost support. Clegg emphasized that these factors were more significant than his policy decisions, particularly on tuition fees. Some critics have referred to Clegg's statements as a blame game, with a Conservative source labeling him as someone who blames everyone but himself.

The article discusses the versatility and beauty of camellias, highlighting their striking combination of polished evergreen foliage and colorful flowers, which bring life to winter gardens. Camellias are reasonably easy to grow, thriving in acidic, free-draining soil, but they are sensitive to alkaline or neutral ground. If the soil isn't suitable, camellias can be successfully grown in containers with ericaceous compost.

The article also mentions that camellias can be pruned to keep them compact and can be trained on walls, arches, or even grown as hedging. Tender kinds like C. reticulata make excellent conservatory plants. Camellias grow well in both sun and shade, and their flowering season is extended, making them a perfect addition to gardens.

The article suggests potted camellias may not last as long as those in the ground, but they can be easily propagated through root cuttings, with the best time for this being between September and February. The article also provides information on choosing and caring for specific camellia varieties, such as Adolphe Audusson, Alba Simplex, Williamsii

The article features photographer Timothy Bouldry who has been capturing images of life at the Boragaon landfill, one of the largest dumping grounds in India. The landfill is home to approximately 100 families who sift through waste daily, searching for valuable materials to sell. Despite the challenging and unsanitary conditions, Bouldry describes the community as content, loving, hopeful, and not jaded by modern civilization. Bouldry's work extends beyond photography, as he also helps improve living conditions for the residents by teaching English, yoga, and cultivating gardens with organic waste. This project forms part of Bouldry's humanitarian photography focus, which he finds the most fulfilling despite the relatively unappealing nature of landfills.

A rapist stalked three women in Leeds city center before chosen his victim, an 18-year-old girl, who was brutally attacked at a bus stop. The attacker, described as of Pakistani or Middle Eastern background, in his early twenties, and slim with a receding hairline, was caught on CCTV wearing a green Puma sweatshirt, dark jacket, and jeans. A woman named Lizzi Crawford, weighing 20 stone and known for her unhealthy diet of takeaways and alcohol, was mistaken for being pregnant on a bus by a child. An article by CNN reveals that African cities such as Lagos, Luanda, Dar es Salaam, and Accra are experiencing significant growth in the number of millionaires. This growth has led to increased demand for luxury goods, with Nigeria being a fast-growing market for French Champagne, digital televisions, and high-end products. A hotel owner, Jennifer McGirr, is living in fear after her windows were smashed and she received threatening phone calls following her appearance on Channel 4's 'Four in a Bed'. After removing his uncomfortable new shoes due to a painful big toe during a Betfred World Championship match against Craig Steadman, Ronnie O'Sullivan, a five-time World Championship winner, had to borrow a pair of shoes from a Crucible audience member. A coronial inquest found that a teenage girl who disappeared in Sydney 40 years ago, Marian Carole Rees, likely ran away and may still be alive. The inquest revealed that Rees had expressed intentions of running away from home, which was supported by evidence that she said goodbye to her brother on the morning she went missing. The inquest also noted that due to the ease of assuming a new identity forty years ago, it is possible that Rees could be living under a new identity. The case has been referred back to the Missing Person's Unit for further probe, as the magistrate found holes in the initial investigation. The missing girl would now be 53 years old. Rees was said to be upset due to her responsibility of taking care of her younger siblings, as her mother had a drinking problem, and was reportedly fed up with her normal life, often expressing a desire to run away.

A mother of three working as an assistant director at a KinderCare childcare center has been charged with child endangerment for allegedly dangling her two-year-old son over a 10-foot-deep cheetah enclosure at the Cleveland Metroparks Zoo. The incident occurred on Saturday afternoon, during which the child slipped and fell into the pit. Witnesses report that the parents leapt into the pit to rescue the child, who was treated for a leg injury. The child is currently in stable condition. The mother, Michelle Schwab, has taken a leave of absence from her position at KinderCare, and the company is conducting an internal investigation into the incident. Unrelated zoo visitors have expressed shock at the parents' actions, believing the cheetahs may have been scared off by the commotion.

A study conducted at the University of Reading found that chewing gum helps reduce the frequency and intensity of earworms, or sticking songs in one's mind. Researchers asked 98 volunteers to listen to catchy tunes like Play Hard by David Guetta and Payphone by Maroon 5, then tasked them to hit a key every time they thought of the songs, while either chewing gum, not chewing gum, or tapping their finger. The results showed that volunteers thought of the song less often and heard it less in their minds while chewing gum, suggesting this technique could potentially stop other intrusive thoughts. More research is needed to confirm this and explore its potential applications for conditions like obsessive-compulsive disorders.

Oregon couple Jesse and Melissa Meek announced their pregnancy in a rap video set to the theme of '90s TV show 'The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air.' The clip, featuring the couple rapping while driving in a car, has been viewed over 1.7 million times on YouTube. Arsenal, currently Europe's form team, are preparing for their Premier League game against Burnley with an eccentric pre-game playlist. Ed Miliband's US advisor, David Axelrod, masterminded two presidential election victories for Barack Obama and is currently helping shape Miliband's cost-of-living and tax fairness strategy. In North Charleston, South Carolina, a white police officer, Michael Slager, shot and killed an unarmed black man, Walter Scott, following a traffic stop for a broken taillight. The community's response was more subdued compared to that in Ferguson, possibly due to the police force in North Charleston being more racially diverse. However, some argue racial profiling may have been a factor in Scott's stop. The outcome of Slager's trial remains uncertain.

An 81-year-old woman living in sheltered housing in Newport was served a poorly prepared baked potato and corned beef meal, which her son, Steve Ashton, found in her refrigerator. A 71-year-old pensioner named Richard Curry from Loveclough in Lancashire was fitted with a magnetic nose after his original one was removed due to a rare form of cancer. Lisa Courtney, a 26-year-old woman from Hertfordshire, has the world's largest collection of Pokemon memorabilia, having amassed over 25,000 items since her interest began at nine years old. The brothers plan to return to Ireland together as soon as possible.

The article reports that Ventura County prosecutors have refiled murder charges against Jane Laut, who is accused of killing her Olympic medalist husband David Laut in 2009. The trial has been postponed multiple times, and prosecutors have accused the defense of withholding discovery. A British nuclear submarine, HMS Talent, suffered £500,000 in damage after colliding with a floating ice patch while tracking Russian vessels, according to The Mail on Sunday. The incident occurred last year, and the submarine is currently out of action for several months for repairs. The incident occurred during heightened tensions between Britain and Russia in the North Sea and Arctic Circle regions, with Russia increasing its submarine activity by 50% in the past 18 months. Previous incidents of submarine damage have been attributed to ice, but later found to be caused by enemy vessels. HMS Talent, a 5,300-ton "hunter-killer" submarine equipped with Tomahawk cruise missiles, cameras, and thermal imaging periscopes, has a history of operational issues. The exact details of the crash, including the location and time, have not been disclosed.

A study has found that consuming two cups of coffee daily could potentially reduce the risk of breast cancer returning by half, particularly for women who are currently undergoing or have completed tamoxifen treatment. The study suggests this could be due to coffee's interaction with breast cancer cells, specifically caffeine, which could slow down cell division and increase the likelihood of cell death, especially when combined with tamoxifen. Notably, this is not the first research to link coffee consumption with improved cancer outcomes; previous studies have shown associations with reduced risks of liver and skin cancer.

Authorities in greater Sydney, Australia are planning to control a observed surge in the population of wild rabbits, considered a pest, through a program of strategically placing carrots laced with the Calicivirus, also known as Rabbit haemorrhagic disease (RHD). This virus, which kills up to 100% of infected rabbits, is aimed at reducing the population to prevent damage to agriculture, environment, and native wildlife. The program has been implemented annually for nine years, and this year will be carried out in May across ten areas, including Sydney and the Central Coast. Homeowners are advised to vaccinate their domestic rabbits to protect them from the virus. Rabbits were introduced to Australia by British settlers.

Medical leaders warn of a potential recruitment crisis, as the shortage of doctors persists in many parts of the country.

Hull KR have signed Australian forward Dane Tilse from Canberra Raiders on a two-and-a-half-year deal as a replacement for the departed front row duo Michael Weyman and Ryan Bailey. A 6-year-old girl's teeth condition deteriorated to a potentially fatal extent due to neglect by her father, Kenneth Wanamaker Jr, who pleaded guilty to reckless endangerment in Northhampton County, Pennsylvania. A 16-year-old transgender boy, who has been struggling with gender dysphoria since childhood, has been granted permission by a Brisbane-based judge to undergo testosterone treatment to transition into a male body. The teen had considered suicide and went to extreme lengths to hide his male identity, including binding his chest and starving himself. The family court process in Australia requires a series of assessments by doctors and psychologists, an official diagnosis of gender dysphoria, and a determination that the child's wishes for hormone treatment reflect an independent and stable choice, following the Gillick competency test. The court process is seen as necessary, but some critics, including a Family Court Chief Justice, have suggested that it may be possible to streamline the process, allowing parents and doctors to make decisions about transitioning without court intervention.

A light aircraft crashed in the Punta Cana region of the Dominican Republic, resulting in seven fatalities, with reports suggesting two British citizens were among the passengers. The pilot was attempting an emergency landing when the plane struck a golf course adjacent to the airport, bursting into flames. The Augusta National Golf Club has implemented a cell phone ban during the Masters tournament, prompting fans to revive old cameras, such as digital and 35mm models. She subsequently shared the test with her followers, urging them to ensure they're in the right relationship. Some commentators viewed the prank as a warning sign, but Allie defended herself as merely trying to entertain her boyfriend and be funny.

Ocean photographer Lloyd Meudell captures the stunning and dream-like moment ocean foam explosions occur on the shores of Kiama beach in New South Wales, producing images reminiscent of surrealism works. He suggests that aspiring photographers familiarize themselves with the ocean before starting their photography journey. Despite being asked numerous times for his camera settings, Meudell keeps these a secret, urging others to explore and learn for themselves. His unique shots can be found on his website, with an unexpected demographic of elderly ladies among his buyers.

Bayern Munich manager Pep Guardiola blames injuries for his team's Champions League quarter-final first-leg defeat by Porto, who took a 2-0 lead after early goals from Ricardo Quaresma and Jackson Martinez, with a second-half effort from Martinez. Porto manager Julen Lopetegui expresses hope for a semi-final spot, urging his team to be "perfect" in the second leg. Martinez, returning from injury, scored two goals and troubled Bayern's defenders throughout the match. Quaresma also praised Porto's team ethic for their victory.

The Curiosity Rover has discovered multi-colored, mineral veins on Mars, located at a site called 'Garden City' on the slopes of Mount Sharp. These veins, ranging from 2.5 inches tall, are believed to have formed from fluids moving through cracked rock in Mars' wet past, with both bright and dark materials present. Scientists believe these veins provide insights into Mars' watery past, suggesting the planet once had more water than the Arctic Ocean and the water existed for over 1.5 billion years. However, over time, Mars has lost 87% of its water, leaving it barren and dry. The study led by scientists at Nasa's Goddard Space Flight Center, is the first to provide estimates of just how much water Mars had in its past, and Curiosity is continuing to explore Mount Sharp to find more clues about the red planet's history.

A 25-year-old man named Carl Bradey sustained severe burns on his entire body after rescuing a three-year-old girl from a house fire caused by a candle in his rental property. The incident left Bradey with nerve damage in his right arm and unable to feel anything. He is currently staying with his mother, recovering from multiple surgeries including skin grafts and vein removal. His family has set up a crowdfunding page to support Bradey in rebuilding his life. Fire experts advise using candles in solid holders away from flammable objects. The house has since been demolished due to asbestos found in the property.

An invasive bacterium, xylella fastidiosa, is threatening olive oil production in southern Italy, particularly in the Puglia region, after infecting thousands of olive trees and causing a 35% drop in production last year. The European Union is alarmed by its spread and France has announced a boycott of Puglian produce, leading to expected shortages and higher prices worldwide. The Italian government's strategy of removing infected trees is met with resistance from growers who argue it won't contain the bacteria's spread. The bacterium has infected 800,000 trees in the Salento area of Puglia and is a significant supplier of virgin olive oil to various countries, including the USA, Austria, Brazil, Canada, China, Korea, Japan, Hong Kong, India, Russia, and Singapore.

A border guard was killed and ten others injured in a cross-fire incident with militants at the Saudi-Yemen border, marking the first known military death for Saudi Arabia since launching airstrikes against rebels in Yemen. Houthi rebels took over the presidential palace in the southern Yemeni port city of Aden, with Yemeni special forces, loyal to former President Ali Abdullah Saleh, reportedly trying to secure the city. Additionally, U.S. Navy warships are patrolling off Yemen to monitor suspicious shipping, particularly any potential weapons shipments from Iran to Houthi rebels. The overall situation in Yemen remains complex and volatile, with hospitals struggling to provide supplies amid ongoing fighting.

A 53-year-old man named Muhammed Tahir was convicted of sexual assault after rubbing himself inappropriately on a young woman on the London Underground. The incident, which was witnessed by undercover police officers, left the victim "frightened and shocking". Despite the judge considering a custodial sentence necessary, Tahir was given a six-month prison sentence suspended for two years, a 12-month supervision order, 150 hours of unpaid work, an £80 victim surcharge, and a five-year ban from using the London Underground during rush hours. The ban was enforced after Tahir's previous similar offense in 2003 was cleared due to the prosecution file failing to arrive in court in time.

A Californian man named Robin Barton, who was abandoned as a baby and later rescued by Santa Ana police officer Michael Buelna from a dumpster in 1989, met Buelna for the first time since the incident. Barton was adopted by a couple from Orange County and his adoptive parents were glad to meet Buelna, the man who saved Barton's life. Buelna was also abandoned by his mother as a child and hopes to help Barton in his search for his biological mother.

A 16-year-old student named Courtney Brain was given a detention for missing half an hour of lessons due to an emergency GP appointment for a water infection. Her mother, Jane Burnham, criticized this decision as "petty and unreasonable", claiming that Courtney has a strong academic record and helps with after-school activities. The school argued that the detention was intended to help Courtney perform well in her upcoming exams. The school's statement also noted a growing concern about students missing vital lessons for medical appointments and requesting that such appointments be made during non-school hours whenever possible.

Graeme Finlay, a 53-year-old former naval serviceman, was acquitted of assaulting two elderly passengers on a cruise ship after an incident over insulting behavior at dinner. He claimed self-defense, saying he was attacked first with a hot chocolate cup and crutch by one of the passengers. The jury returned unanimous not guilty verdicts for charges of unlawful wounding and inflicting grievous bodily harm. Finlay said he would never set foot on a boat again due to the stressful ordeal.

Hayley Carney, a transgender woman living in the U.S., is planning to move to the UK to marry her unidentified fiancée, Anne, who resides in Plymouth, Devon. Carney aims to become a British citizen and fulfil a lifelong dream, believing the UK is more accepting of her identity. She will undergo gender transition surgery before the move and will apply for a marriage visa after arrival, setting her on the path to citizenship. Carney has long been fascinated by Britain and feels more at home there due to perceived cultural acceptance.

1. Atletico Madrid manager Diego Simeone has expressed surprise at the absence of English teams in the Champions League quarter-finals this season, attributing it to a lack of performance and citing the potential and financial prowess of the Premier League.
2. Simeone, preparing for a crucial quarter-final second leg against Real Madrid, believes that despite the strong talent and financial conditions in the Premier League, Spain's La Liga still houses the two best teams in Europe, observed by Madrid's and Barcelona's dominance in the competition.
3. In the first leg of their quarter-final, Atletico empathically held Real Madrid to a goalless draw, positioning them well for the second leg, which Real will be playing without key players Karim Benzema, Gareth Bale, Luka Modric, and suspended defender Marcelo.

David Cameron and Boris Johnson, aiming to promote Tory plans for expanded childcare, struggled with a children's seasonal jigsaw puzzle at a day nursery in Surbiton. The puzzle proved more challenging than anticipated, with Boris Johnson attempting to force pieces together and proposing the slogan, "If in doubt, wedge it in." After a young child pointed out several errors, the pair found success in a finger painting activity. Their campaign visit encountered delays and was somewhat overshadowed by their puzzling difficulty.

Justice Diana Bryant, a top judge in Brisbane, proposes the regulation and legalization of commercial surrogacy in Australia to prevent instances of child abandonment, particularly in the light of recent cases like Baby Gammy. She believes that this would allow for ethical terms and oversight of such arrangements, rather than having hopeful parents enter into unlawful overseas surrogacy deals. If legalized, she suggests that strict requirements would be imposed to ensure the well-being of the children and respect for biological parents' identities.

A seven-storey fall survivor, aptly named 'Seven', has been on the road to recovery at My Vet Animal Hospital after being found injured and covered in maggots in Zetland, inner-east of Sydney. 'Seven' sustained serious injuries, including a broken jaw, broken leg, broken hard palate, and bruised lungs. The cat's story of survival captivated the hearts of many, resulting in donations to help pay for its extensive medical bills and surgeries. After learning to walk again at the vet clinic, Seven is now ready for a new home in about six weeks.

MasterChef UK crowned its eleventh series winner, Simon Wood, a data manager from Oldham, who prepared an impressive three-course meal consisting of octopus, squab pigeon, and lemon posset to win the title. After 7 weeks of tough challenges, he was commended for taking ordinary dishes and making them special by judge John Torode. Tony Rodd, an architectural recruitment consultant from London, and Emma Spitzer, a managing director of a luxury travel business, were the other finalists. In a separate news item, Kim Woodward, a former MasterChef semi-finalist, became the first woman to be appointed head chef at the Savoy Grill, a prestigious restaurant in London with a 126-year history, where she previously worked as a sous chef between 2010 and 2012.

Hull City manager Steve Bruce acknowledges the need for 'crazy results' to preserve their Premier League status, as they prepare to face Southampton with only a two-point cushion above the relegation zone. The unpredictable nature of the season is highlighted, with meetings still to come against high-profile teams like Liverpool, Arsenal, and Manchester United. Bruce is confronted with a decision about the form of goalkeeper Allan McGregor, who has made errors in recent games, with the experienced Steve Harper and midfielder Tom Huddlestone set to return for the Tigers. In this crucial match against Southampton, highly-rated by Bruce, the team will need to perform near their best due to the Saints' strong overall performance this season.

Celebrity chef Bobby Flay is reportedly offering his ex-wife, actress Stephanie March, a monthly sum of $5,000 as per their prenup, despite his net worth exceeding $20 million. The prenup also stipulates that he can buy out the $8 million marital home for $1 million, with an additional $50,000 for moving expenses. March is reportedly unhappy with the financial terms of the prenup. The couple, who have no children together, separated three weeks ago and are currently in the process of divorcing. Their marriage allegedly started to deteriorate over the past year and a half, with incidents such as Bobby not visiting Stephanie when her appendix burst and him attending a wine festival instead of celebrating their 10th wedding anniversary.

Leading Australian modeling agencies are now focusing on 'insta-fame' as a criterion for hiring models, with the rise of social media necessitating the addition of 'influencer' and 'blogger' divisions to their traditional model portfolios. These divisions cater to the growing demand from clients for models with high social media followings, alongside conventional requirements of beauty, fitness, and health. General Manager of Vivien's Models, Catherine McGill, confirmed that they have launched an 'influencers' section due to this trend, with the minimum expectation of clients ranging between 10,000 to 300,000 followers. Agencies like Chic Management are also capitalizing on this trend by managing bloggers and influencers, with a focus on the 'cool girl' appeal that is a strong draw for clients. This combination of 'cool girl' status and a substantial social media following is reportedly what is currently attracting clients, with models undergoing training on self-promotion through Instagram. Popular American model Alexis Ren, with over 1.6 million followers, is an example of this blending of traditional modeling and social media influence.

Hungarian architect Matyas Gutai and his collaborator Milan Berenyi have built a prototype house using a "liquid engineering" system in Kecskemet, Hungary. This innovative house utilizes a sheet of water trapped between inner layers to maintain a consistent temperature throughout the building, with excess heat being stored for later use when needed. The house is able to reheat itself, produces its own energy, and is more independent of traditional energy suppliers, making it a sustainable and efficient solution. Gutai began developing this concept while studying sustainable architecture at the University of Tokyo in 2003, inspired by open air hot baths. The house's design and materials have been refined to address potential issues like the freezing of water and the breaking of panels. The goal is to use less energy and materials and move cities off-grid, with the introduction of water houses as a step towards a greener future.

Cardiff City have returned their allocation of 500 tickets for the Championship game against Leeds United at Elland Road, citing a matter of principle, after the Welsh club were offered fewer tickets than their November visit. The clubs have a history of fan trouble, and Leeds have not commented on the decision for such a low number of tickets, which was believed to be down to the club, council, or police. Cardiff's CEO has criticized the travel and ticket restrictions, stating that West Yorkshire Police could manage the event without issue or restrictions, if they chose to do so. The Cardiff City Supporters Club Chairman has expressed support for the decision, citing improved behavior from fans in recent years. The Elland Road game will now be without any away fans, and Cardiff have rejected Leeds' request for a 'beam back' at the Cardiff City Stadium.

Utah photographer Alan Lawrence, after initially feeling negative emotions upon learning that his newborn son Wil had Down Syndrome, now finds that Wil brings joy to the family and has opened new opportunities. Lawrence has created a photo series titled 'Wil Can Fly', depicting Wil appearing to fly, which he shares on his blog and social media. The aim of these photos is to raise awareness about Down Syndrome, and proceeds from a calendar featuring these photos will be donated to two Down Syndrome foundations. Wil's unique behavior of pretending to fly as a baby inspired the series, and Lawrence plans to continue photographing Wil in different locations to further spread awareness.

In Egypt, eleven football fans have had their death sentences upheld after a retrial regarding the 2012 stadium riot between Al-Masry and Al-Ahly, which resulted in 74 deaths. The riot erupted after a league match between the two clubs, leading to days of violent protests in Cairo. The appeals court upheld the sentences and referred the cases to the grand mufti for a final decision on May 30. The 73 defendants include police officers, club officials, and fans. The riots were the deadliest in Egypt's history, and games were played behind closed doors due to fan violence.

In the Ghanaian slum of Nima, a local mosque provides a venue for weekly coding classes for young girls, led by tech entrepreneur Regina Agyare. This initiative, part of Agyare's mentorship program "Tech Needs Girls," aims to empower these girls, many of whom face social barriers to education, and give them a voice through technology. Achievers Ghana, a non-profit organization supporting the education of local girls, partners with this mosque to provide extracurricular classes and school funding. The integration of boys into the classes is also deliberate, as Agyare aims to challenge traditional gender expectations and equip the future generation with a more inclusive perspective. The ultimate goal is not to turn every girl into a software developer but to help them reach their full potential and bring change to their community.

The traditional "Original Pig Rassle" event at St. Patrick's Parish in Stephensville, Wisconsin, which involved mud-wrestling pigs, has been cancelled after complaints about animal mistreatment. The church has decided to replace the 44-year-old tradition with a human mud foosball tournament. Global Conservation Group, an animal advocacy organization, launched an online petition accusing the church of inhumane treatment of the pigs and garnered over 81,000 signatures. The church has stated that they are moving towards less controversial areas to better utilize their talents. Both the church and the animal advocacy group have expressed satisfaction with the changes.

Tennis players Maria Sharapova and Venus Williams have withdrawn from their countries' Fed Cup ties due to a leg injury for Sharapova and personal reasons for Williams. Sharapova was forced to withdraw from Russia's semi-final against Germany, while Williams pulled out from the USA's World Group play-off against Italy. In Sharapova's absence, the Russian team will depend on players like Anastasia Pavlyuchenkova, Svetlana Kuznetsova, and Elena Vesnina, with captain Anastasia Myskina needing to find a replacement for Sharapova. The USA will be led by Serena Williams in the World Group play-off against Italy, with Lauren Davis replacing Venus Williams.

A 36-year-old woman from Gary, Indiana, suspected of posing as a Child Protective Services employee, has been taken into police custody on suspicion of kidnapping and murdering a 23-year-old mother, Samantha Fleming, in Anderson, Indiana, with the intent to steal Fleming's three-week-old daughter, Serenity. Fleming disappeared with her baby on April 5, and her body was found at a residence in Gary on April 17. Remarkably, Serenity has been found safe and is expected to be returned to relatives in Anderson. The suspect, now under mental health care in a Texas hospital, had a nursery prepared in her home and is believed to have known a significant amount of personal information about Fleming.

An Ohio woman, La-Sonya Mitchell-Clark, discovered her biological mother, Francine Simmons, worked at the same call-center company and lived only six minutes away after the Ohio Department of Heath released birth records. Upon receiving her records, Mitchell-Clark found Simmons on Facebook, connected the dots, and reached out through social media, leading to a phone call and eventually meeting. The reunion also included Mitchell-Clark discovering she had three biological younger sisters. The parents and siblings were supportive, and Mitchell-Clark's adoptive parents were also understanding of her search for her biological parents.

An Icelandic duo has created a protein-rich energy bar named Jungle Bar, which includes cricket flour as a major ingredient. Claimed to be a good source of protein and other essential nutrients, the bar is also free from gluten, peanuts, dairy, and soy. The creators hope their product will encourage western diets to incorporate more insect-based food, aiming for a shift towards a more sustainable and conscious food culture. The Jungle Bar is currently available for pre-order through Kickstarter, with expectations for shipping to begin in August 2015. The duo gained previous attention for their Fly Factory, a project that breeds insect larvae for human consumption, which could potentially contribute to addressing global food shortages.

A 73-year-old reserve deputy, Robert Charles Bates, mistook his pistol for a stun gun during an undercover drug operation and fatally shot 44-year-old Eric Courtney Harris. Harris was attempting to buy a gun and drugs from undercover deputies in a Tulsa, Oklahoma dollar store parking lot. Bates, who is classified as an advanced deputy, had been monitoring the situation from afar and ran up to try to de-escalate the situation, leading to the fatal shooting. Harris was accused of attempting to sell drugs and a sawed-off gun to undercover officers as part of an ongoing methamphetamine investigation.

A Russian unmanned spacecraft, Progress 59, bound for the International Space Station lost contact with flight controllers and is expected to re-enter Earth's atmosphere between May 5 and May 7. This re-entry will not pose a threat to the ISS as its orbit differs significantly from that of the space station. The Progress vehicle carries more than 3 tons of supplies for the ISS, but the hitch will not affect the six-member ISS crew, as the lost supplies are not critical to the operational segment of the station. Efforts are ongoing to re-establish contact with Progress 59.

Hull City manager Steve Bruce has revealed that players will face up to a 50% salary reduction if the team is relegated, due to financial provisions set up to protect the club. The team, currently in 17th place with a tough run-in, has the third-lowest total wage bill in the Premier League. Bruce has praised the job done by Alan Pardew at Crystal Palace, whom Hull face this weekend, but empathizes that they need to end a two-month winless streak. Mo Diame, who has been out for five months with a knee injury, continues to suffer from pain and is doubtful for the match.

Leo Schofield, a 79-year-old restaurant critic and festival curator, expressed feelings of bitterness and depression following a decade spent living in Tasmania. He relocated back to New South Wales after the Tasmanian Government reduced funding for his Baroque music festival by 25%. Despite initially moving to Tasmania with the intention of showcasing its heritage, Schofield criticized Tasmanians for wanting to exploit the land, prompting a negative response from Luke Martin of the Tourism Industry Council of Tasmania. Martin denied the cuts to Schofield's funding and labeled his comments as 'blatant mistruths'.

The photography competition held in conjunction with the Northern Territory Cattlemen's Conference showcases the unique outback lifestyle, people, and landscapes of remote Australian regions. The winning entry, "True Love" by Marie Muldoon, is a touching photo of a girl embracing a horse, capturing the strong bond between humans and animals in rural areas. The competition aims to foster connections between rural and urban communities, as described by Tracey Hayes, the CEO of the Northern Territory Cattlemen's Association. Previous winners include Jacynta Coffey in 2014 with "Trucking," embodying typical station life, and Tania Brooks with "Noo Noo and Toby," showcasing a notable human-animal relationship.

The book "Sex by Numbers" explores various sexual statistical claims to separate myths from realities, focusing on penis size measurements. The latest study, involving 15,521 penis measurements from worldwide participants, indicates that the average erect penis size is approximately 5.2 inches in length with a 4.6-inch circumference, with the most accurate measurements being made by trained health professionals. Additionally, the book addresses other sexual misconceptions, such as the duration of intercourse, the impact of physical exercise on erections, the relationship between baldness and sexual drive, the average number of erections per day, and more.

Barnet Football Club returned to the Football League after a two-year absence following a 2-0 win against Gateshead in the Conference, with Mauro Vilhete scoring two goals. This win sealed the Conference title for Barnet, ensuring manager Martin Allen's fourth spell in charge would be his most successful. Gateshead played defensively throughout the match, with Barnet dominating the play. Although there were close calls for Gateshead, ultimately, Barnet won the match, securing their promotion and avoiding drama on the finale.

Remains of a missing college freshler, Anjelica 'AJ' Hadsell, 18, have been found 40 miles from her home in Norfolk, Virginia. The remains were found outside a residence in Franklin and have been sent to the Chief Medical Examiner's Office for identification and to determine cause of death. Investigations including the FBI are ongoing, with no evidence of foul play initially reported, but concerns among family and friends persist as Hadsell vanished on spring break from Longwood University. Hadsell's stepfather, Wesley Hadsell, was previously arrested for breaking into a home, claiming he was searching for his missing stepdaughter.

The article discusses rumors that Apple plans to address the 'bend gate' issue with the iPhone 6 and iPhone 6 Plus by using stronger materials for its next generation smartphones. This may include the use of 7000 series aluminum, a material used in competition bicycles and the Apple Watch Sport edition. This alloy is said to be 60% harder than standard alloys. The upcoming iPhones, expected to be called the iPhone 6S and iPhone 6S Plus, may also include the A9 chip, Force Touch Feature, and a possible four-inch version called the iPhone 6C. The article cautions users to avoid putting excessive pressure on the middle of the phone to prevent bending.

The article discusses the state of European rugby, where English clubs have not won the top prize in eight years. While four English teams are in the last eight of the new Champions Cup, bookmakers predict holders Toulon and Clermont as the main contenders. The article highlights significant challenges for English teams, including substantial funding disadvantages compared to French teams, and the superior recent European pedigree of Leinster. After reviewing the prospects of each team, the article suggests there is a fair chance that one English team might advance to the next round, with Bath and Saracens being the likely candidates. If two English teams made it, it would be a significant boost to national morale.

A New York-based teacher named Sam Pearce has combined his teaching career with a modeling job, working for top designers such as Alexander McQueen and DKNY. He was discovered on a subway in New York City and signed with RED NYC modeling agency. Despite his busy schedule, Pearce maintains that his teaching responsibility is his priority and plans to help his students through fundraising. He believes in himself as a teacher who models rather than a model who teaches.

An amateur astronomer, Gordon Ewen, captured a unique image of a sun spot that resembles a chick sitting on the sun's surface. This phenomenon is fairly common and occurs due to a concentration of magnetic fields causing a reduction in temperature on the sun's surface. These sun spots can range in size from 10 miles to 100,000 miles and can be seen from Earth without a telescope. Sunspots have a temperature lower than the surrounding solar material, which makes them visible. They are also the source of solar flares and coronal mass ejections (CMEs). The photograph was taken using Ewen's telescope that focuses on a specific wavelength of light. He set up an observatory shed in Letchworth, Hertfordshire, after leaving his job five years ago.

Vladimir Putin is allegedly planning to utilize the threat of nuclear war to defend the Crimean peninsula from being reclaimed by Ukraine and potentially expanding Russian control into NATO-bordered Baltic states, according to notes from a top-secret meeting between American and Russian officials. The notes suggest Russia will respond forcefully, including through nuclear force, to perceived threats from NATO. Tensions between Russia and NATO are currently high due to the ongoing conflict in eastern Ukraine and the annexation of Crimea, with the latter being a flashpoint that could lead to nuclear war. The imminent threat is thought to be towards the Baltic states, prompting concerns and military preparations from NATO members Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania.

Virgin Galactic aims to test a new version of SpaceShipTwo by the end of the year, following the crash of its predecessor in the Mojave Desert in 2014. The new spacecraft is nearly ready and could begin test flights by year's end, according to CEO George Whitesides. The old spacecraft was destroyed when co-pilot Michael Alsbury accidentally activated the feathering system at high speeds, leading to the disintegration of the craft. The new spacecraft is designed to address the lessons learned from this crash and ensure it performs better.

A refugee couple in Cloverdale, Perth, are left distraught after an alleged racial attack by a neighbor, who verbally abused them with racist slurs and swung a crowbar, resulting in a violent confrontation. The incident, captured on video, has prompted their children to question their identity, asking if they are "really monkeys." The 51-year-old woman accused of the attack maintains she was the victim, feeling that the refugee family should not be in Australia. She has since been charged with multiple offenses, including assault, going armed in public, disorderly conduct, and racially harassing conduct. However, the woman has claimed she was scared for her life during the encounter.

Walmart is under scrutiny after a stolen rifle from their Tuscon, Arizona store was used in a shooting incident by thief Mario Valencia. Despite store employees claiming the gun was properly locked, video evidence shows the rifle's wire was loose, allowing it to be fired. During a chase, Officer Michael Rapiejko hit and apprehended Valencia with his vehicle. Valencia is facing multiple felony charges for a crime spree, including theft, vandalism, burglary, home invasion, and auto theft. Rapiejko was initially put on administrative leave but was later reinstated after being cleared of any wrongdoing.

A father-of-five, identified as Peter Kelly, was fatally stabbed following a three-hour verbal altercation with three other fishermen at the St Croix River in Wisconsin. Kelly and his friend, while fishing on the Minnesota side, asked the rowdy fishermen on the Wisconsin side to be quieter, which escalated into a heated argument. The attackers fled the scene after the stabbing, and authorities are still searching for them, with descriptions of the men and their vehicles provided. The community is mourning the loss of Kelly, a volunteer coach at the high school's football, baseball, and wrestling teams, who leaves behind his wife and five children all under the age of nine.

Holly Willoughby and Davina McCall have teamed up for their first joint campaign, promoting Garnier Nutrisse hair dye. In the shooting, they pose playfully with moustache-like hairstyles. Holly has chosen the shade 10.01 as her perfect match, while Davina prefers 4.3. Besides this collaboration, Holly has recently launched a vintage-inspired clothes range for babies, and Davina renewed her wedding vows with her spouse of 15 years in Las Vegas. They also recently went on a road trip with their children in California.

The baby boomer generation's approaching deaths may result in a wave of funeral debt for their children and grandchildren, according to a report. Deaths in the UK are anticipated to increase by 20% over the next two decades, reversing a 40-year trend of decreasing mortality rates. The cost of a funeral has risen by 80% over the past decade, with a "simple" funeral now costing an average of £3,590, while a more elaborate service could cost as much as £5,423. The report suggests that many families will struggle to cover these costs as they stand, with more than half of UK households having less than £3,000 in savings.

The Transportation Security Administration's Aviation Security Advisory Committee found that nationwide full screening of airport employees would not significantly lower overall public risk due to its inability to determine a person's intent to cause harm. Instead, the report advised a risk-based, multi-layered security approach that includes strengthening employee vetting, expanding the collection of domestic intelligence, and enhancing criminal background checks. Following the arrest of a ramp worker and passenger for allegedly smuggling guns onto flights, TSA Secretary Jeh Johnson announced immediate actions, such as increased random screening of aviation employees and increased access point security.

Raheem Sterling and Jordon Ibe were pictured smoking a shisha pipe, an incident similar to past controversies involving Jack Wilshere, who has been embroiled in a smoking row after being spotted with a cigarette and shisha pipe. Diego Maradona was suspended from football for 15 months due to cocaine and drug abuse, Saido Berahino was filmed inhaling 'hippy crack' while driving, and Kyle Walker was forced to issue an apology for inhaling 'hippy crack' during a night out. The article also mentions Paul Merson, who struggled with drink, drugs, and gambling, and Robin Friday, a former Reading forward known for his drug-taking, drinking, womanizing, fighting, and smoking, who retired and died young.

The article discusses a Reddit thread involving members of the disabled community sharing instances where well-intentioned actions from able-bodied individuals are perceived as patronizing or offensive. Condescending phrases like "You're an inspiration," "Brave," or "Strong" were commonly criticized for trivializing their experiences. Some found it irritating when others refused to accept their abilities and offered unwanted help, especially when asked not to. Misconceptions about their conditions, such as assuming they were faking their disabilities or recommending treatments, were also highlighted as issues. Lastly, discussing religion in relation to their situations was met with strong disapproval. The consensus was that simple respect and acknowledgment of their autonomy was what they desired most.

A German engineering team has developed a concept car named EOssc2, modeled after crabs to navigate tight urban parking spaces. The EOssc2 can turn on the spot, shrink in size, and move sideways. It's designed as a flexible micro-car for mega cities, equipped with semi-autonomous driving capabilities. The car can link with others to form a connected convoy, aiming to save energy during long-distance travel or car-sharing schemes. After three years of development, a team of 10 engineers has built the EOssc2, which is currently being tested in Bremen, Germany, and Dalian, China. The car features inbuilt cameras and a LIDAR sensor on its roof for scanning the environment and locating itself.

Middlesbrough secured a 2-0 home win over Rotherham United, with goals from Lee Tomlin and Patrick Bamford, keeping their automatic promotion hopes alive. The home side dominated the game, with Bamford scoring the opener in the second half and Tomlin providing the assist. Despite the victory, Middlesbrough remained fourth in the Sky Bet Championship table as the top three teams also won.

The Tewksbury Police Department in Massachusetts was targeted by hackers using the CryptoLocker malware, which encrypted vital records on their computer network. The department was forced to pay a $500 ransom in Bitcoin to restore access to their data, as the most recent back-up was corrupted. This observed incident of ransomware attack is not a data breach, as the information remains within the department's control, but the malware encrypts the data, making it unreadable. This unfortunate event is not isolated, as similar attacks have occurred at other police departments in the U.S.

A Chinese woman named Zhu Diandian, whose surname translates to "pig" in Mandarin, has gained internet fame for her unique bond with her 187lb pet pig, Five Flowers. The pair sleep together, and Zhu often posts photos of them on social media, including selfies of her in bed with the pig. Her husband is reportedly tolerant of the relationship, but her pet dog shows signs of jealousy. Zhu works at a publishing company in Beijing and has nearly 40,000 followers on Weibo, where her posts of Five Flowers have received thousands of likes and comments.

A woman, Louise Smith, secretly pulled two hairs from a young girl's head and planted them in her food at the Crown and Thistle pub in Cumbria, intending to get the meal for free as she couldn't afford the £21 bill. Smith was convicted of fraud in her absence at Carlisle Magistrates' Court this week. The pub has stated that they prioritize food hygiene and child welfare, and an arrest warrant has been issued for Smith, who is now on the run.

Thailand's Kiradech Aphibarnrat won the inaugural Shenzhen International, claiming his second European Tour title in a play-off. Initially, 19-year-old Chinese teenager Li Hao-tong, who carded a closing 67 to finish 12 under par, seemed set to secure a home win, as Aphibarnrat trailed by two shots with two holes to play. However, Aphibarnrat holed from 18 feet for an eagle on the 17th, and despite missing a potential winning birdie on the last, he clinched victory in the play-off, hitting his approach to virtually the same place as in regulation and holing the birdie putt after Li missed from long range. Aphibarnrat had previously won in the Malaysian Open in 2013, and expressed his relief and joy, especially dedicating his success to his late coach Natpasit Chokthanasart.
