The killing of three-year-old Mikaeel Kular by his mother Rosdeep Adekoya, despite a history of concerns and social service visits, could not have been predicted by the care teams involved. Adekoya was jailed for 11 years last August after pleading guilty to culpable homicide and attempting to defeat the ends of justice. An independent significant case review has concluded that the circumstances leading to Mikaeel's death could not have been predicted, but identified areas for future learning and action to improve practices. The full report is not being published to protect personal information.

Victoria Wasteney, a senior occupational therapist and born-again Christian, has launched an appeal against the East London NHS Foundation Trust after receiving a written warning for praying for a Muslim colleague and inviting her to church events. The incident occurred in 2013, resulting in Wasteney's suspension for nine months, and a subsequent three-complaint ruling finding her guilty of misconduct. The lawyer for Wasteney argues this action restricts her freedom of conscience and religion as provided by Article Nine of the European Convention of Human Rights. The case could have broader implications for the right to express religious beliefs in the workplace. Wasteney is represented in court by human rights barrister Paul Diamond and has the support of the Christian Legal Centre.

Chelsea moved closer to winning the Premier League title with a hard-fought 1-0 victory against Manchester United, thanks to Eden Hazard's goal in the 38th minute. Jose Mourinho's side extended their lead at the top of the standings. In the match, Branislav Ivanovic had a tough time marking Marouane Fellaini, but he did well in the air throughout the game. Notable performances included John Terry's strong performance against Radamel Falcao, Cesar Azpilicueta's quiet loss-side performance, and Oscar's brilliant back-heeled assist for the goal. Mourinho was given a 7/10 rating for his tactical approach, which managed to stop United, a task which many others have struggled with in recent weeks. Manchester United struggled to create chances, with Juan Mata's set-piece delivery rarely finding its intended target and Radamel Falcao being bullied out of the game by Terry.Louis van Gaal was the manager of Manchester United and was given a 6/10 rating for his performance. Eden Hazard was named Man of the Match.

Three men aged 50s, all local residents of York, have been arrested today on suspicion of the murder of missing chef Claudia Lawrence, who vanished in 2009. The arrests mark a new development in an investigation that has continued since, with two other suspects previously arrested and released without charge. North Yorkshire Police have launched a fresh search for evidence related to Lawrence's whereabouts, with the searches anticipated to continue for several days. The public and the Lawrence family are urged to maintain patience as police carry out these crucial investigations. Previously unseen CCTV footage and multiple searches have been conducted since Lawrence's disappearance, but her body has still not been found.

A 92-year-old woman named Pamela Clothier returned from a hospital stay to find her home in Battle, Sussex, empty of her possessions, including her beloved dog Mitzy, after her son gave the charity Age UK permission to clear out the house under the impression that she planned to sell it. Clothier has criticized her son for his actions and called for changes in the law to make it more difficult for charities to act without the homeowner's permission. The charity Age UK has apologized for the ordeal and said it has reviewed its procedures to prevent similar incidents from happening in the future. Critics say more should be done to protect the elderly and their assets.

The article discusses the events surrounding a fire that broke out at Paul's Hair World in Manchester's Northern Quarter on July 13, 2013, which led to the death of firefighter Stephen Hunt. A 16-year-old girl was initially charged with arson due to discarding a cigarette that allegedly caused the fire. However, the judge dropped the charges after determining that the girl was 'guilty only of being careless'. The prosecutor suggested that the combination of damaged cardboard boxes and the girl's careless act could have led to the fire. The article concludes by mentioning the impact of Stephen Hunt's death, with more than 1,000 people attending his funeral in September 2013.

Sofia Vergara's attorney has stated that the actress, currently engaged to Joe Manganiello, has no intention of destroying or using the frozen embryos she created with ex-fiance Nick Loeb. Vergara prefers to keep the embryos frozen indefinitely as she has no desire to have children with her ex. The fate of the embryos is currently in dispute following a lawsuit filed by Loeb seeking a judge's order to prevent Vergara from destroying the embryos. The couple created the embryos in November 2013, six months before ending their relationship.

A planned auction of 450 WWII internment camp photos and artifacts has been canceled following protests, including by actor George Takei and the Heart Mountain Wyoming Foundation. These groups argued that the items are significant to the history of Japanese-American incarceration and should not be sold. Allen Eaton, the collector of the items, would have opposed the sale, as evidenced by a Change.org petition and claims that the collection was meant for a public exhibition rather than auction. The Rago Arts and Auction Center acknowledged the controversy and the ethical questions surrounding the sale of such historical items.

The article reports on the tragic murder of Stephanie Scott, a 26-year-old English and drama teacher, who went missing just a week before her wedding. Police charged a man with her murder, despite not finding her body, leaving her loved ones to plan the funeral and continue the search. Her family and friends, who traveled from around the world for her wedding, are now facing the difficult task of attending her funeral. Stephanie was last seen at her workplace on Easter Sunday, where she was excitedly making final preparations for her wedding with her fiancé Aaron Leeson-Woolley.

The Science Channel's new series, Chaos Caught on Camera, premiering on April 13, showcases raw and unfiltered footage captured by individuals during various real-life or death-defying situations, including a devastating tornado in Illinois, a deadly collision of skydiving planes, and a battle between a lion and a buffalo in South Africa. Each episode deconstructs the incidents with graphics, illustrations, and explanations of the facts. Remarkable moments captured in the series include a diver finding a rescued survivor in a boatwreck and an impala jumping into an open car window to escape a cheetah. The series aims to provide a raw, intense experience for viewers as if they're in the disaster-zone.

In a futuristic vision imagined by artist Alex Brady, space travel includes extravagant space stations similar to Las Vegas, complete with casinos and neon lights, accessible by various space planes. These space stations, comparable in size to small cities, would provide artificial gravity and a bustling, chaotic atmosphere reminiscent of Earth's cities. The designs incorporate efforts from European, American, and Indian space programs, with single-stage-to-orbit vehicles potentially making travel to these stations more accessible. However, these images are meant as a light-hearted, tongue-in-cheek depiction of the future of space travel, not a strictly serious prediction of its possibilities.

Tim Sherwood, Chris Ramsey, and Les Ferdinand built a strong friendship during their time working at Tottenham's Youth and Under 21 programs from 2008. After leaving Tottenham, Sherwood and Ramsey continued their bond, although temporarily Put on hold, due to Sherwood blocking Ramsey's calls. In the current Barclays Premier League season, they will be opposing managers, with Sherwood at Aston Villa and Ramsey at Queens Park Rangers. If Ramsey's tenure at QPR proves short-lived, Sherwood hinted that he would ask to bring him to Villa Park. They are credited with nurturing some of the club's most promising young talents, including Harry Kane, Andros Townsend, and Ryan Mason. The trio's influence on the development of these players has not gone unnoticed, with England Under 21 midfielder Alex Pritchard and Joshua Onomah, the captain of Tottenham's youth team, being notable examples.

Actors are in demand for voiceover work, with some reportedly earning up to £50,000. This type of work can boost their income, but it can also cause tension with their major employers, as actress Katy Cavanagh found when she was reprimanded for doing voiceover work for BBC iPlayer Restart in her role on Coronation Street. The soap's bosses were reportedly disgruntled as the advert could be seen as promoting a competitor, EastEnders. In the past, Coronation Street has reportedly tried to discourage its stars from doing voiceover work for television adverts. Executive at soap executives have reportedly just overturned a ban on their cast offering their dulcet tones to radio advertising campaigns after rumours of a near-mutiny among its actors, the catalyst for which was Katy's extensive voiceover work.

Voiceover work can be a lucrative side gig for actors, with names such as Benedict Cumberbatch, Olivia Colman, and Shane Richie lending their voices to various campaigns. Cumberbatch has worked with Jaguar and Pedigree dog food, while Colman has

Three British men who were arrested for plane spotting in Dubai and Abu Dhabi are to be freed after spending two months in prison. Conrad Clitheroe, Gary Cooper, and Neil Munro were stopped by police for writing down aircraft registration numbers at Fujairah Airport, accused of espionage, and held despite being told they would not be detained. A defense argument that they were pursuing their passion for plane spotting and had no ill intent led to the charges being dropped. Mr. Clitheroe, who has a heart condition, will soon be able to return home to celebrate his first wedding anniversary with his wife Valerie. The families had been concerned about the men's welfare while in custody and were relieved to hear that they will be released without charges.

The F-35 Lightning II jet is equipped with a $400,000 helmet that provides a 360-degree view and real-time battlefield information to the pilot, thanks to six infrared cameras. This high-tech headgear, which projects critical data like airspeed, altitude, and warnings onto the visor, has faced issues such as poor handling of turbulence, motion sickness, communication problems when multiple jets are involved, and a green glow that obscured night vision in early versions. Despite these problems, the F-35 is considered one of the most complex pieces of military hardware due to its 8 million lines of software code, making it a potentially game-changing asset in aerial combat.

In the latest ComRes poll, the Conservatives have gained a four-point lead over Labour with 36% of the vote, while Labour stands at 32%, Ukip at 10%, Liberal Democrats at 8%, and the Greens at 5%. The poll indicates that over one in five voters are undecided regarding their choice, with both main parties receiving around 48% of potential support. The poll also shows a significant decline in support for the Liberal Democrats, with only 41% of their 2010 voters possibly considering voting for them again. Additionally, the poll suggests that Conservative voters are less enthusiastic about the rise of smaller parties, with 46% fearing that another hung parliament might give small parties too much power.

James Holmes, a former neuroscience Ph.D. student, is on trial for the 2012 shooting in a Colorado cinema during a midnight showing of "The Dark Knight Rises," in which he allegedly killed 12 people and injured 70 others. Holmes' legal defense is insanity, claiming he was in a psychotic episode during the shootings. If convicted, Holmes faces the death penalty. The jury selection for the trial is ongoing, with an 11-member jury and 11 alternates, mostly white and middle-aged individuals. Victims and their families are advocating for media outlets to stop using the names and likenesses of mass shooters to deny them media attention. Holmes' family describes him as a brilliant but troubled individual, with a history of mental health issues.

The Premier League leaders Chelsea host Manchester United on Saturday, with the latter aiming to challenge for the title following a six-game winning run. Chelsea's key player Eden Hazard could face competition for the PFA Player of the Year award, contending with United's David de Gea, who has been in top form this season. Luis Van Gaal's United are set to be missing Angel di Maria due to his poor form, with Juan Mata likely to take his spot in the starting eleven. This weekend's match may see a clash of the two biggest egos in football, as Jose Mourinho and Louis van Gaal face off once again. United will be aiming to upset Chelsea's title charge, with a victory potentially leaving them just five points behind the leaders. The Colombian players Falcao and Cuadrado, signed for big money last season, have struggled to make an impact and are unlikely to start on Saturday.

Glenn Mason, a former NatWest bank manager, has admitted to stealing £185,000 from elderly customers to fund his internet gambling addiction. He was jailed for 15 months in November 2018 and now plans to pay back the entire amount from his RBS pension pot. The bank had already refunded the targeted customers and will receive the money as compensation. Mason's actions negatively affected the community, and his victims expressed feelings of mistrust towards banks after his crimes.

In a survey by Ripley's Believe It or Not, Britons voted David Beckham as the celeb they'd most like to have as a father, while Holly Willoughby was chosen as the preferred mother figure. Unusually, the Osborne family, Sharon and Ozzy, were voted second for both parents. The survey also revealed that Ed Sheeran and Channing Tatum would be the ideal brothers, and Adele and Rhianna as sisters. The study considered extended family as well, with Helena Bonham Carter as the top choice for aunt and David Walliams for uncle. Results showed that trust and kindness were more important than wealth or looks when choosing a parental figure.

In South Africa, violence has broken out between immigrant gangs and locals, with at least five deaths reported since anti-foreigner attacks began two weeks ago in Durban. Immigrants have taken refuge in police stations and armed themselves for self-defense. The government and African National Congress party have condemned the violence, with President Zuma calling it a violation of South Africa's values. Foreigners have been targeted in Johannesburg and other areas, forcing more than 2,000 to flee to camps protected by armed guards. The US ambassador to South Africa has spoken in defense of the immigrants, while leaders and officials have called for an end to the violence towards foreign nationals. Police have responded to the violence by firing tear gas grenades and searching hostels for weapons.

Royal Dutch Shell Plc has lodged a complaint in federal court in Alaska, seeking an order to remove Greenpeace activists who scaled and occupied the Polar Pioneer oil rig in the Pacific Ocean. The activists, from various countries, climbed aboard the rig, 750 miles northwest of Hawaii, as it was en route to the Arctic. They plan to unfurl a banner with the names of millions of people opposing Arctic drilling. Shell believes the activists' actions are illegal, jeopardizing both the safety of the crew and the protesters themselves. The activists aim to draw attention to oil drilling in the Arctic and oppose Shell's plan to drill for oil in the region.

A fashion photographer, Ian Pettigrew, is presenting a series of portraits featuring 56 adult women living with cystic fibrosis (CF) to bring hope and awareness to those affected, particularly children and teenagers. In his upcoming book, Salty Girls, Pettigrew showcases women with the disease, which causes thick mucus in the lungs and digestive system, to demonstrate the strength and beauty of those battling the condition. One of the models revealed struggles with body image issues, but chose to participate in the project to empower young people living with CF. Pettigrew aims to inspire hope for a brighter future among younger generations with the help of his photographs.

Bruce Jenner, now 65, revealed in a two-hour ABC special that he started a gender transition process in the mid-1980s, including hormone therapy, electrolysis, and plastic surgery to feminize his features. However, he halted the transition after meeting Kris Kardashian and marrying her in 1991, a decision he attributed to fear and shame about publicity. Their relationship led to a 22-year marriage and two children. Jenner's decision to transition was reportedly influenced by the life story of transgender tennis player Renee Richards, who won the right to compete as a woman in the 1977 U.S. Open. Dr. Phil, a television psychologist, expressed support for Jenner, saying he needed to be himself to avoid draining his spirit. The interview was conducted before a fatal car accident involving Jenner. His four older children were present for the interview, but Kardashian and Jenner's younger daughters did not participate.

Jamelia, a panelist on Loose Women, faced backlash after suggesting that high street stores should not cater to women larger than a size 20, stating she was referring to people with extreme sizes for health reasons. She claimed her comments were misconstrued and intended to encourage healthier lifestyles for overweight teenagers. Her co-panellists defended her, stating her focus was on unhealthy sizes. However, she later apologized for not making her intentions clear enough. Twitter users criticized her comments, with some stating she should be sacked from the show. Despite this, she supports a campaign for self-esteem on social media.

England dominated a farcical warm-up match against St Kitts Invitational XI, with Jos Buttler, Mark Wood, and Alastair Cook standing out. The match was draw, but it was a meaningless contest with both teams performing poorly. England's performance indicated that Gary Ballance might be a concern, and the focus is now on deciding the second spinner between Adil Rashid and James Tredwell. The poor performance of St Kitts showcases the steep decline of Caribbean cricket, and this match was an example of the inconsistencies in modern cricket scheduling.

On the opening day of The Masters Tournament at Augusta National, 21-year-old Jordan Spieth set a new record as the youngest first-round leader with a spectacular round of 64. Justin Rose, 34, and Ernie Els, 45, tied for second with a score of 67, while Charley Hoffman also scored 67. Notable players like Rory McIlroy, Bubba Watson, Dustin Johnson, and Phil Mickelson trailed behind the impressive Texan, who dominated the day with a fabulous run of six birdies in seven holes and a 25-foot birdie putt at the 18th. Spieth, who finished runner-up last year, now leads the tournament by three strokes going into day two.

An axe-wielding robber named Shaun Andrew McKerry, who has a history of over 1,000 offenses since the age of 11 and was once dubbed "Boomerang Boy," was subdued by a husband and wife duo during an attempted post office robbery in County Durham. The shop owner, Sab Dhillon, tackled McKerry while his wife hit him with a baseball bat. CCTV footage of the incident shows Dhillon removing McKerry's scarf to reveal his face to cameras. Despite initial fear of the unknown criminal, Dhillon and his wife were unaware of McKerry's extensive criminal history at the time.

A Ryanair flight attendant named Fernando Miguel Andrade Viseu stole a £500 camera left on a flight and listed it on eBay. The camera's owner, primary school teacher Aaron Galloway, found the listing while searching for a replacement and messaged Viseu, who confessed to the theft. Viseu was charged with theft, admitted his guilt in court, and was sentenced to attend a drug rehabilitation program, pay costs, and perform 100 hours of unpaid work. Ryanair has since terminated him. Galloway was disappointed that Ryanair did not seem to have sufficient security measures in place to prevent such thefts.

This article discusses Julie Creffield, a runner who was discouraged by doctors and hecklers from running a marathon while she was a size 18, but went on to complete the marathon and numerous other races. Despite two-thirds of women claiming they can't run, often due to self-consciousness and fear of judgement, Creffield aims to encourage women to take up running through her website, The Fat Girl's Guide To Running. She appeared on This Morning alongside sub-three hour marathoner Nell McAndrew to launch the show's Run For Your Life campaign. The campaign aims to show that anyone can find success with running and improve physical and mental health, particularly for women who may feel self-conscious or unfit.

Passengers on Cruise Ship Carnival Spirit experienced a two-day ordeal at sea, trapped due to severe storms in Sydney Harbor. The storm resulted in huge waves as high as 40 feet, leaving many passengers seasick and traumatized. The ship docked at the Overseas Passenger Terminal Wednesday morning, with passengers expressing relief to disembark. The ship is expected to set sail again later in the day for a 7-day cruise. Waves up to 11 meters have been recorded off-shore throughout the ordeal, causing minor damage to the ship.

Jessa Duggar, a 22-year-old star of the TV show "19 Kids & Counting", announced that she's pregnant with her first child with husband Ben Seewald. The due date is November 1st, which is also their wedding anniversary. The couple is known for their pro-life stance and large family, with Jessa being the third child to marry and every marriage resulting in a baby in the first year. No birth control is used, as Michael Duggar stopped taking birth control after a miscarriage and decided only to leave family planning to God. The baby will be the sixth grandchild for the Duggars. Jessa and Ben are excited to become parents and are still planning to adopt, despite the requirement of being married for two years by the adoption agency they've contacted. The news does not come as a surprise, as an image of the couple was uploaded to Facebook suggesting they could be expecting.

A team of three students at Rice University has developed a new device called Comfortably Numb, which, within 60 seconds, numbs the skin prior to an injection by producing a rapid chemical reaction to cool the patient's skin. The device costs around $2 (£1.34) to produce and consists of two sealed chambers containing the chemical ammonium nitrate and water. The team is currently in the process of applying for a provisional patent for the device and hopes to continue working on it in their second year. The device could potentially be used for procedures like tattoos and piercings.

The article discusses the media's trend of referring to Hillary Clinton, the 2016 presidential candidate, as "Hillary" casually, similar to how pop stars are known by their first names. This contrasts with how male political figures are typically addressed with their first and last names.The article argues that this casual approach diminishes the formality and respect needed for the position of the U.S. president, potentially reinforcing gender stereotypes. Clinton's campaign's use of "Hillary" on its website and in communication is also analyzed as potential attempts to make her seem more personable or to distance her from negative stereotypes.The article emphasizes that it is essential for the American public to be able to imagine electing a female leader who is respected, not just liked, and that this formality helps maintain that necessary distance between the president and the public.

1. During the Coachella music festival, Madonna kissed Drake on stage for at least three seconds, prompting a visible reaction of discomfort from the 28-year-old artist.
2. Despite the unsettled look on Drake's face, sources laterclaimedhe enjoyed the kiss, but was merely put off by Madonna's lipstick.
3. Madonna, aged 56 and wearing a provocative outfit, surprised many at the festival known for attracting a younger crowd, reminiscent of her kiss with Britney Spears at a music award show 12 years prior.

A jockey previously perceived as a popular journeyman, Leighton Aspell, won the Crabbie’s Grand National at Aintree for the second consecutive year on Many Clouds, beating AP McCoy who was aiming for a fitting conclusion to his record-breaking career. The win marked Aspell's first success in back-to-back National races since Bryan Marshall in 1953 and 1954. Many Clouds had a rough start to the season with a disappointing Cheltenham Gold Cup finish, but passed the finish line nearly one-and-a-half lengths ahead of 33-1 shot Saint Are. The race saw 19 out of 39 horses complete, with jockey Aidan Coleman's horse, The Druids Nephew, showing promise before falling at the 26th fence, and AP McCoy's mount, Shutthefrontdoor, finishing fifth. Despite McCoy's failure to secure a win in his final Grand National, the victory of Many Clouds provided a significant triumph for trainer Oliver Sherwood and owner Trevor Hemmings, who has previously won the race with Hedgehunter in 2005

In a hacked Sony email, PR Peggy Siegal expressed concerns that the 12 Years A Slave director, Steve McQueen, would not win the Best Picture Oscar because the Academy alleged the film, directed by a British man, depicted a negative view of America that wouldn't be well-received by its mostly white, patriotic members. the emails also suggest a future Hollywood movie based on Dr Who is in development but won't be released for several years. The emails were part of a database leaked from Sony Pictures Entertainment by hackers in November 2013.

Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei has demanded an immediate lifting of all sanctions in parallel with any final agreement on curbing Iran's nuclear program. In a speech, Khamenei voiced concerns about US deception and expressed reservations about reaching a deal at all. He warned against any 'extraordinary supervision measures' over Iran's nuclear activities, including foreign inspections of military sites, which he claimed would not be allowed. The U.S. State Department has maintained its stance that sanctions would be lifted gradually, only upon verification of Iran's compliance with specific commitments.

A woman named Ranette Afonso is set to marry Marko Conte, the man who crashed into her car in August 2013 while she was waiting for her husband. They fell in love and began dating shortly after her divorce. The pair, who share a mutual passion, exchanged insurance and contact details following the accident and began texting regularly. Marko proposed on their third date just two months after the accident, and they are planning to marry this October. Ranette's close family supports her decision, though some friends found it surprising due to the speed at which the relationship developed.

A remote Iron Age fort built by the Picts on a 20-foot-high sea stack in Scotland has been discovered. The fort, which appears to have been built with stone imported from elsewhere in the country, may have been one of a number lining the east coast of Scotland. The small fort, found on Dunnicair sea stack, offers a strong defensive position despite the challenges in resupplying it up the cliff faces. The fort's walls and a hearth inside the fort, with charcoal still present, suggest it was lived in for extended periods, indicating its importance. The Picts, a group of tribes who lived north of the Forth and Clyde during the Late Iron Age and Early Medieval period, were known for sea raids. The archaeologists found rough Pictish carvings on some of the stones used to build the fort's walls, and believe the site may have been a precursor to Dunnottar Castle. The team now hopes to examine the charcoal and other artifacts found at the site for a better understanding of who lived there.

A Texas A&M, Galveston professor, Irwin Horwitz, emailed his strategic management class of about 30 students to inform them that he was failing the entire class due to their disruptive, disrespectful, and unprofessional behavior, including cheating, during the semester. Horwitz's decision to fail the class, which he has taught for 20 years, was criticized as extreme, but he defended his actions as a response to a toxic learning environment. However, the university has stated that they will re-evaluate the across-the-board failing grades and will not allow Horwitz to give students failing grades without academic justification. The course will be taught by the department head for the rest of the semester, and grades will be based on academic performance. Horwitz has expressed reluctance to teach the class again at the Galveston campus.

A woman, Laura Everley, was diagnosed with an aggressive ovarian tumor after recognizing her symptoms, such as bloating, back pain, constipation, and frequent urination, in a Facebook post about ovarian cancer. She had initially attributed her symptoms to irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) or endometriosis. Following her hysterectomy, doctors discovered that the cancer had already spread. She is currently undergoing chemotherapy, and with treatment, doctors are optimistic about her chances of recovery. Everley hopes her experience will raise awareness of ovarian cancer symptoms, which can be challenging to recognize due to their similarity with less severe conditions.

A blonde waitress named Agnese Klavina has gone missing from a popular club in Puerto Banus, Costa del Sol, and a property developer's son, Westley Capper, is being questioned in connection with her disappearance. Capper admitted driving Klavina away from the nightspot but is suspected of illegally detaining her by police who have studied footage from the club's car park. The investigation is ongoing, and DNA tests are expected to be ordered on human hair and samples taken during a search of a motorboat belonging to Capper's family. The case has been given international attention, and Klavina's friends and family are seeking justice.

Gavin Thorman, a notorious drug kingpin, was jailed for 12 years after being caught discussing his illegal drug operation from prison, where he was serving time for assault. He boasted about his planned expenditure on cosmetic surgeries and luxurious items, but was unaware that his conversations were being recorded by police. The operation, which involved 26 members of the same gang, was one of the largest in North Wales, with authorities seizing Drugs worth nearly £200,000, luxury cars, guns, and even a boat. Thorman was sentenced as part of a five-year painstaking investigation codenamed Operation Yonside, which was set up to combat organized crime gangs. The case resulted in the most significant sentencing in the region, with the 26 defendants receiving a total of 127 years imprisonment.

A 21-year-old Australian named Chris Ball, who struggled with depression, made a heartbreaking goodbye video to his family before taking his own life. In the video, he tells them not to blame themselves and categorically states that no one could have prevented his death due to depression being a disease. His devastated family has decided to make the video public in an effort to raise awareness and the funds for more beds for suicidal youths in hospitals. Chris's mother, Kerrie Keepa, who has lost multiple family members to depression, believes her son could still be alive if he had not been sent home from Redland hospital 11 days before his death, due to a lack of available beds. Kerrie is now advocating for emergency suicide training in hospitals and more beds for suicidal youths, as part of a petition to the government.

The self-proclaimed mastermind of the Gone Girl-inspired kidnapping of Denise Huskins in California has threatened to 'go overseas and teach English' or 'live off the grid and read books for the rest of my life' if authorities do not grant immunity to his co-conspirators. In a lengthy email sent Saturday, the kidnapper group claimed they were behind a series of burglaries and car thefts, used squirt guns disguised as firearms, and had monitored Huskins' boyfriend Aaron Quinn while pretending the incident was a hoax. After a statewide search involving numerous law enforcement agencies, Huskins was found safe in Huntington Beach just a few hours after her alleged kidnapping. Attorneys for both Huskins and Quinn have confirmed aspects of the kidnapper's email and provided evidence to support its authenticity. However, neither the Vallejo Police Department, the FBI, nor their respective attorneys have publicly commented on the emails.
